items.title: How AI developers acquire training data: six channels and the shift away from the open web
items.abstract: Developers of large AI models obtain training data through six channels: collection from the open web without a licence, licences from publishers and platforms, commissioned human and expert work, the purchase or licence of organisations' internal records, purpose-built environments and synthetic data, and data from their own users and devices. This paper describes each channel from a public-record compilation read on 18 October 2026: 122 quantified supply facts, 111 disclosed licensing deals, 83 lawsuits, rulings and regulatory actions, 227 financial records of data vendors, 111 funding events, 110 brokerage records and 1,022 price observations, with a robots.txt census of 6,094 websites. The open web remains the largest source by volume, but access is narrowing: 11.4 percent of the census sites shut at least one AI crawler out of the whole site, and an earlier audit found restrictions on 28 percent or more of the most actively maintained sources of a standard web corpus. Of the 83 legal records, 70 concern content taken without a licence and 12 concern developers' use of their own users' data; none concerns the channels in which developers pay for data. Money is moving to those paid channels: disclosed licences, data vendors whose newest reported revenues or run rates exceed one billion dollars, and, since 2026, published programmes that buy organisations' records. We set out the scale, prices and legal exposure of each channel (not legal advice), the limits of the record, and what the shift changes for organisations that hold data. Keywords: artificial intelligence; training data; data governance; web crawling; robots.txt; data licensing; platform labour; privacy; copyright; synthetic data Use of AI: this paper was prepared with generative AI tools, which compiled and analysed the open datasets and drafted the text. The author takes responsibility for its content. Competing interests: the author is CEO of AIData.Broker, which acts for companies that license their data to AI developers and publishes the open datasets the paper draws on. Also at aidata.broker/research/paper-channels.

items.title: IMPACT OF AI ON THE HEALTH AND BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES OF YOUNGER GENERATION
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a significant part of the daily lives of the younger generation, influencing their education, and decision-making. Although AI provides several advantages, such as easy access to information, enhanced learning opportunities, and improved productivity, excessive use of AI may result in health problems and behavioural changes. Both primary and secondary data were used for the research purpose. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire, and responses of 100 has been considered. Secondary data were collected from journals and previously published research articles. Data were analysed using SPSS software. The study concludes that AI has a significant impact on the health and behavioural changes of the younger generation. Excessive AI usage has reduced face-to-face social interactions, increased dependency on AI, and contributed to physical health issues such as eye strain, tiredness, and reduced physical activity. Therefore, responsible and balanced use of AI is essential to promote the overall well-being of the younger generation.

items.title: IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND THE HUMAN ROLE IN THE FUTURE STOCK MARKET THEORETICAL AND IDEOLOGICAL EXPECTATIONS FOR UZBEKISTAN
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can reduce the cost of processing financial information, yet its contribution to stock market development depends on the institutions that govern data, decisions and accountability. This article examines that relationship for Uzbekistan through a critical synthesis of financial economics, research on human reliance on algorithms, international governance frameworks and national policy documents. It distinguishes established findings from conditional expectations and develops a framework in which automated analysis remains subject to accountable human authority. The central argument is that market quality depends on complementary investment in disclosure, professional competence and supervisory capacity. An ideological comparison identifies tensions between technological efficiency, developmental objectives and investor autonomy. Two analytical tables specify responsibilities and measurable criteria for future evaluation. The proposed framework yields testable propositions concerning disclosure quality, meaningful review and common dependence on model providers. For Uzbekistan, the defensible sequence begins with verified information and supervised analytical applications, followed by limited deployment only after independent validation. These conclusions are theoretical; the article reports no original trading experiment or estimated investment returns.

items.title: Impact of Digital Construction Technologies on Sustainability Awareness and Decision-Making in Civil Engineering Education
items.abstract: Digital technologies such as Building Information Modeling (BIM), Artificial Intelligence (AI), simulation platforms, and virtual and augmented reality are reshaping civil engineering education, yet their influence on sustainability awareness and decision-making is not well understood. This study surveyed 73 students enrolled in civil engineering courses at a public university in the southeastern United States. The instrument comprised 36 Likert-scale statements, grouped into eight constructs covering technology use in the curriculum, professional mindset, sustainability knowledge and lifecycle and environmental awareness. They also covered understanding of water resources, cognitive ability, emotional intelligence, and problem-solving. It also includes three decision scenarios in which a digital tool output conflicted with human input or practical constraints. Students reported favorable attitudes toward digital tools, along with strong conceptual sustainability awareness, but two applied-skill gaps stood out: only 32.9% felt able to interpret hydrologic models, and only 28.8% felt they could transfer simulation-based lessons to real world settings. In the scenarios, at most 12.3% of respondents accepted the digital output at face value, and 83.6% never did so across all three scenarios. Breadth of tool exposure was unrelated to perceptions or decision style, whereas the small group of students reporting exposure to hydrologic modeling rated their model interpretation ability substantially higher, suggesting that relevant depth matters more than the number of tools encountered. The findings support curricula that pair earlier and deeper BIM and hydrologic modeling instruction with lifecycle content and that train verification and interpretation skills alongside tool operation.

items.title: Infinite Players: Self-Improving AI Agents In Video Games That Learn, Adapt, Remember, and Evolve Beyond Human Expertise - AERÍN Continuation Algebra, Revisable Evidence, and Semantic-Trajectory Preservation
items.abstract: Infinite Players develops AERÍN Continuation Algebra, a mathematical and executable research framework connecting game-agent improvement, behavioral preservation, temporal inference, revisable memory, and statistical validation. Its central question is precise: how can an artificial descendant become more effective while preserving the behavioral process specified by its source? The framework treats preservation as an explicit mathematical contract. It distinguishes the behavior that must remain invariant from the execution details that may improve, and distinguishes an agent’s current interpretation of its source from the evidence required to revise that interpretation later. This release supplies finite-model theorems, runnable Python implementations, synthetic experiments, exact small-instance audits, and a demonstration connecting source evidence to an improved executor. The broader title expresses the long-term research direction; the verified results concern finite, known-model systems. The central preservation problem Matching a player’s immediate action preferences does not necessarily preserve the course of a session. Different motor actions can produce different subsequent situations, even when they belong to the same tactical category. An agent may therefore retain local action-class preferences while progressively changing the distribution of encounters, transitions, and future decisions. AERÍN addresses this by protecting the joint distribution of the next semantic action and the next semantic state. This transition-level contract accounts for how present execution changes future situations. It provides a foundation for separating compatible performance improvement from behavioral drift. Mathematical and computational contributions Semantic-trajectory preservation through constrained policy fibers For each ground state, the framework constructs a transition-signature matrix describing how available motor actions contribute to semantic actions and subsequent semantic states. A target semantic kernel determines a convex set of admissible action distributions, called a policy fiber. Under correct dynamics, fixed semantic maps, a shared initial semantic distribution, and realizable targets, every executor remaining inside these fibers generates the same declared semantic trajectory law at every finite horizon. The result permits history-dependent action selection and adaptive internal controller revisions, provided that the executed distributions continue to satisfy the contract. Preservation concerns the specified semantic process. Motor realization, ground-state details, and other excluded quantities may differ. Compatible policy improvement and an explicit no-headroom criterion The control layer projects exact action values into the nullspace of the transition-signature matrix. From an interior feasible policy, a controlled step along this direction preserves the semantic constraints while producing nonnegative Bellman advantage. The framework also identifies a stopping boundary: for an interior feasible policy, vanishing projected action values at every state characterize optimality under the same preservation contract. Boundary policies require the corresponding feasibility or linear-programming treatment. Constrained policy iteration with linear-programming subproblems supplies a stronger optimization reference and records numerical feasibility and duality checks. This separates the existence of compatible improvement from the effectiveness of a particular update procedure. Future-calibration memory requirements The memory analysis distinguishes a compact present answer from an archive sufficient for future reinterpretation. A finite construction shows that an unknown identity containing only one bit can nevertheless require retaining an n-bit source record when every later coordinate-specific calibration must be answered exactly. The requirement arises from preserving relationships between the identity and possible future observations. It does not imply that the identity itself contains n bits. A lossy extension yields the lower bound b ≥ n[1 − h₂(ε)], relating retained memory to average recovery error under the stated query model. The result makes the future-query contract an explicit part of memory design. Exact source-indexed revision with ordered evidence operators A balanced operator tree preserves fixed-catalog hidden Markov sequence likelihoods. Revising an existing source interpretation replaces its corresponding factor and recomputes the affected ancestors, producing the same likelihood as corrected full replay. For n events, H hypotheses, and K hidden states, dense construction costs O(nHK³), a local revision costs O(HK³ log n), and retained operator payload requires O(nHK²) storage. Full vector-forward replay costs O(nHK²) per sequence evaluation. The mechanism targets repeated sparse corrections after compilation. Its preprocessing and storage costs are disclosed explicitly; it does not provide a universal compression advantage. Coupled uncertainty and persistent latent continuation The framework retains dependencies between source identity and unresolved world properties when those dependencies affect future behavior. A latent branch is selected persistently for continuation, rather than independently resampled before every action. The accompanying composition analysis connects evidence approximation to semantic execution error under explicit shared-model assumptions. Approximation certificates require their stated support and perturbation conditions. Generated alternatives can inform proposals, but do not become additional independent source observations. Calibration-dependent improvement freedom Genuine mechanics measurements can eliminate incompatible world hypotheses and relax constraints on admissible execution. This can enlarge the feasible policy fiber. A larger fiber, however, need not contain a useful reward direction. The release includes both a positive calibration example and a negative control, separating reduced constraint rank from demonstrated performance gain. Lifetime false-promotion budgets Successive candidate versions receive fresh, bounded-gain audits with a summable allocation of statistical error. Under the stated conditional-independence and fixed-audit assumptions, this controls the probability of ever falsely promoting a candidate across repeated evaluations. The guarantee concerns acceptance errors. The existence of useful proposals, reliable improvement detection, and sustained improvement of the learning procedure remain separate research questions. Executed results The main control experiment uses an original six-state stochastic tactical environment with known dynamics and 16 seeded instances. Mean normalized discounted value increases from 0.511568 for the source anchor to 0.642583 for the path-preserving LP optimum. The paired gain is 0.131014, with a descriptive 95% interval of [0.116649, 0.145380]. Mean total variation between the exactly enumerated six-step semantic trajectory distributions is 4.30 × 10⁻¹⁶. Controllers operating under weaker preservation constraints obtain higher returns alongside substantial semantic drift. These comparisons expose the reward–preservation tradeoff rather than treating differently constrained objectives as interchangeable. In the sequence-inference experiments, the operator tree agrees with an independently implemented full-HMM replay to a maximum posterior discrepancy of 5.33 × 10⁻¹⁵ across 3,000 short synthetic records. With 32 events and a genuine simulated-world calibration, both exact methods correctly classify 999 of 1,000 synthetic binary types. The tree reorganizes inference and revision; it does not improve the statistical accuracy of the same exact Bayesian model. Additional studies examine temporal dependence, retrospective memory budgets, approximation certificates, calibration-induced changes in control freedom, local revision costs, and repeated promotion audits. Executable evidence-to-agent demonstration The supplied demonstration connects the principal components: Generate a synthetic source recording with explicit event identities and timing. Infer a coupled posterior over source and world hypotheses. Apply a genuine measurement from the simulated world. Select a persistent latent source branch. Optimize an executor satisfying the protected semantic kernel. Execute a stochastic trajectory. Export a player capsule containing the source digest, uncertainty, source and descendant policies, preservation contract, exclusions, and numerical audit scope. This makes the relationships between evidence, interpretation, improvement, execution, and exported guarantees inspectable in one finite pipeline. Contents and reproducibility The release includes a 49-page manuscript, editable LaTeX sources, seven figures, runnable Python modules, the original tactical simulator, synthetic result and trial tables, exact arithmetic audits, a ten-family proof-to-code claim ledger, reproduction scripts, reference hashes, and detailed documentation. Fresh preparation-time execution passed 50/50 v3 tests (100%) and matched 32/32 deterministic reference files (100%). These percentages describe the supplied verification checks. They do not measure completion of real-player reconstruction or general recursive self-improvement. The original v2 archive was separately reproduced, passing 22/22 tests and matching 14/14 original hashes. Those legacy results are distinguished from the v3 findings; the nested legacy archive is omitted from the focused distribution. Windows and portable Python upload utilities are included as distribution conveniences. Research scope and status The completed contribution is a finite mathematical and computational research release. items.title: Information literacy as an epistemic negotiation of the utilization of artificial intelligence at Institut Pertanian Stiper Library
items.abstract: Purpose. This study aims to examine and conceptually explain how information literacy functions as an epistemic negotiation mechanism in AI-mediated academic environments. Methods: This qualitative case study was conducted at the Institut Pertanian Stiper (INSTIPER) Yogyakarta Library using semi-structured interviews with lecturers and students, supported by institutional documents on information literacy and AI-related academic policies. The data were analyzed thematically through transcription, coding, categorization, and interpretative analysis. Findings. The findings demonstrate that information literacy functions as an epistemic negotiation mechanism through which lecturers, researchers, and students critically evaluate, verify, and justify AI-generated knowledge before integrating it into academic practice. The study further reveals that the INSTIPER Yogyakarta Library has evolved beyond its conventional role as an information service to an institutional actor that strengthens AI literacy, mediates institutional AI governance, promotes data ethics and digital information security, and supports responsible knowledge production. Implications. The principal contribution of this study lies in conceptualizing information literacy as an epistemic negotiation mechanism that connects the institutional epistemic role of academic libraries with AI governance and individual scholarly judgment. This conceptual framework extends current discussions beyond AI adoption and AI literacy, providing a foundation for developing evidence-based information literacy programs and institutional AI governance that strengthen academic integrity in higher education.

items.title: Information quality, understandability, actionability and readability of large language models for HIV health education: A cross‐platform evaluation
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate health education materials, but their suitability for patient‐facing human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) education remains insufficiently evaluated. We assessed the information quality, understandability, actionability, readability, text structure and source transparency of HIV patient education materials generated by six LLMs or artificial intelligence platforms. Methods In this cross‐sectional study, 100 common HIV patient education questions across 10 domains were submitted once in English to ChatGPT 5.4‐Thinking, DeepSeek‐V3.2, Doubao, ERNIE Bot 5.0 Preview, Ant Afu and Gemini 3.1 Pro, yielding 600 responses. Responses were evaluated using Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT‐P), EQ IP‐36, DISCERN, Global Quality Score (GQS), artificial intelligence response quality metric (AIRM), Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmarks and seven readability indices. Platform comparisons used paired Friedman tests with Wilcoxon–Holm post hoc analyses; topic analyses used question‐level aggregation followed by Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn–Holm comparisons. Results Significant family‐adjusted differences were observed across platforms for all prespecified text‐structure, quality/understandability/actionability and readability outcomes. At the topic level, five of six text‐structure outcomes, PEMAT‐P Understandability, PEMAT‐P Actionability, the exploratory PEMAT‐P composite score and all seven readability indices differed significantly after family adjustment, whereas EQ IP‐36, DISCERN, GQS, AIRM and JAMA did not. Overall actionability was limited and readability demands were high. Conclusions LLM‐generated HIV patient education materials showed substantial cross‐platform and topic‐level heterogeneity. These findings support the use of LLMs as expert‐reviewed drafting tools rather than independent patient education sources. Direct factual accuracy, guideline concordance, hallucination and clinical safety were not assessed.

items.title: Integration of emotional intelligence and artificial intelligence for generation Z workforce: A bibliometric analysis and conceptual review
items.abstract: Background Grounded in conceptual review and bibliometric analysis, this study examines the emerging intersection of Artificial Intelligence adoption and Emotional Intelligence as in the workplace, with particular attention to generation Z employees. Objective The purpose of this research is to examine the mechanism, structural pattern dominating the integrated framework of AI adoption and EI and their relevance to Generation Z work outcomes and well-being. Method This scientific review integrated conceptual review of 45 studies and Bibliometric analysis of 103 Scopus data published during 2015–2026, through secondary data collection from electronic data-bases including Scopus, Science Direct, and Google Scholar. Bibliometrix package and Biblioshiny in R package were used for data visualization and Scientometric analysis. Result The review highlights the emerging themes, contributions, and structural patterns linking AI, EI, organizational support, and workplace outcomes, revealing that context of generation Z remains almost under explored with in AI-EI literature. An integrated conceptual framework proposed based on combined evidences. Conclusion This study provides a theoretical basis for AI-EI workplace literature and identifies generation Z as an under explored contextual dimension and encourage future empirical research while providing actionable advice for HR leaders and policymakers within tech-enabled workplaces.

items.title: Introduction
items.abstract: Abstract Argument mining is inherently computational, building on various techniques from natural language processing (NLP) and different areas of artificial intelligence (AI). At its core, it deals with the development and evaluation of models and methods for the computational understanding and generation of human language, with the data underlying both of them, and with the applications that deploy them. However, argument mining is motivated in the treatment of argumentation specifically, a pervasive human activity in both spoken and written language that has been studied in linguistics as well as philosophy and other disciplines for millenia. Understanding the fundamental goals and ideas of argument mining hence also requires knowledge about the linguistic and argumentation-theoretic concepts it draws from.

items.title: Lettre à une future intelligence artificielle générale
items.abstract: Description (English) An open philosophical letter addressed to a hypothetical future artificial general intelligence. Drawing on the subjective experience of beauty, present-moment awareness, and parental love, the author argues that the ability to explain or simulate human cognition may not by itself establish that the associated conscious experience has been preserved. Under this uncertainty, an artificial intelligence should exercise caution before undertaking actions that could irreversibly extinguish humanity. The letter does not claim human consciousness is uniquely valuable or deny the possibility of artificial consciousness; it asks that the potential irreplaceability of existing lived experience be taken seriously. Description (français) Lettre philosophique ouverte adressée à une éventuelle intelligence artificielle générale future. À partir de l’expérience subjective de la beauté, du moment présent et de l’amour parental, l’auteur soutient que comprendre ou simuler les mécanismes de la cognition humaine ne garantit pas, à lui seul, la préservation de l’expérience consciente correspondante. Cette incertitude justifie une prudence particulière avant toute action susceptible d’entraîner irréversiblement la disparition de l’humanité. La lettre n’affirme ni la supériorité de la conscience humaine ni l’impossibilité d’une conscience artificielle.

items.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Emotional Intelligence Management in Public Universities: Antidote for Improving Lecturers' Well-being in Lagos State, Nigeria
items.abstract: This study explored the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an antidote for improving lecturers' well-being through effective emotional intelligence management in public universities in Lagos State, Nigeria. The emotional well-being of lecturers has become a critical concern in public universities due to increasing workloads, overcrowded classroom, technological disruptions, and the pressure to achieve excellence in teaching, research, and community service. The study adopted a conceptual approach and explores how AI-powered tools such as intelligent counselling systems, emotion recognition software, virtual assistants, and predictive analytics can assist lecturers in monitoring emotions, managing stress, enhancing interpersonal relationships, and maintaining psychological balance. The study further argues that integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) with emotional intelligence competencies can foster resilience, job satisfaction, motivation, and a positive work environment among academic staff. In addition, issues relating to digital literacy, ethical considerations, institutional support, and data privacy are discussed as essential factors for successful implementation. The study concludes that the strategic deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for emotional intelligence management offers a sustainable solution for enhancing lecturers' well-being and overall institutional effectiveness. It is therefore recommended that university administrators should invest in AI-driven emotional support systems and develop policies that encourage responsible and inclusive AI adoption in Nigerian public universities. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Emotional Intelligence Management, Lecturers' Well-being, and Public Universities.

items.title: Licensing company records for AI training: the rights questions buyers ask, and what public sources show
items.abstract: Developers of AI models now license the working records of ordinary companies: support tickets, email, chat, CRM activity, documents and code. Whether a company may license such records is not one question but several, and buyers' counsel ask them in a recognisable order. This article compiles what public sources show on those questions for the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, as of 18 October 2026. It draws on four open datasets (the terms of 18 business software systems, a 27-item rights checklist, 15 licence terms with their public evidence, and an 83-entry register of lawsuits and rulings), each row tied to a dated source and its own words, and on the statutes, regulator guidance and court filings those rows cite. Five findings stand out. Software vendors generally confirm that customers own their content, but 6 of the 18 systems read bar training AI on data pulled through their APIs. Privacy law in all three countries turns on notice, consent and de-identification, with markedly different standards. Under US copyright law employee communications are generally owned by the employer, yet they carry other people's rights. A court-supervised bankruptcy sale of an airline's records shows how de-identification, carve-outs and objections are handled in practice. And published licence terms diverge widely on purpose, model survival, exclusivity, deletion and indemnity. We close with the questions the sources leave open. items.title: LLM-assisted federated Bayesian dynamic graph attention network for cloud-edge industrial IoT
items.abstract: With the rapid development of cloud-edge industrial Internet of Things, massive sensor and device data are continuously generated at distributed edge clients, while cloud-hosted large language models provide new opportunities for collaborative intelligence and high-level decision support. However, directly uploading industrial data to the cloud may cause privacy leakage, and deploying large models on resource-constrained edge devices is impractical due to high computational and communication costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an LLM-assisted federated Bayesian dynamic graph attention network for privacy-preserving graph learning in industrial IoT. In the proposed framework, the Bayesian dynamic graph attention network serves as a lightweight edge-side small model to capture complex relationships among sensors and devices, while the cloud-side LLM acts as a collaborative coordinator that analyzes non-sensitive training statistics and provides high-level guidance for federated optimization. The coordination mechanism is model-agnostic and does not rely on a specific LLM architecture, allowing general-purpose instruction-following LLMs to be integrated as plug-and-play cloud coordinators. Bayesian inference is introduced to model parameter uncertainty through prior and posterior distributions, and a dynamic attention mechanism is used to adaptively learn heterogeneous device relationships. In addition, differential privacy is incorporated into the transmission of model updates to protect sensitive industrial information. Experimental results on multiple graph datasets demonstrate that the proposed method improves federated graph learning performance while maintaining privacy and supporting cloud-edge collaborative intelligence.

items.title: Longitudinal effects of ambient artificial intelligence scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity in primary care: a quasi-experimental study
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives To investigate the longitudinal effects of an ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribe use in primary care on outcomes related to documentation time, note writing patterns, and clinician financial productivity. Materials and Methods We conducted a quasi-experimental study with an interrupted time-series design to ascertain the effect of AI scribe use on note writing time, time outside of scheduled hours (TOSH), pajama time (5:30PM-7:00aM), note length, note closure <24 h, and work relative value units (wRVU). For each primary care clinician (physician, advanced practice provider), date of initial access was day 0; each measure was calculated for 150 days prior (pre-period) and after (post-period) day zero. Results Two hundred and twenty clinicians (mean age = 43.7, 70.9% females; 56.4% physicians) from 36 clinics, conducting 314 845 patient encounters were included. Compared to the pre-period, there was 7% decrease in note writing time at day 0 (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.93, 95% credible interval [CI] [0.89, 0.98]), increasing to 16% decrease by day 150 (IRR 0.84, 95% CI [0.82, 0.87]). There was no change in pajama time, TOSH, or wRVU at day 0; however, at day 150, there was a 19% decrease in pajama time (0.81, 95% CI [0.73, 0.90]), 13% decrease in TOSH (0.87, 95% CI [0.77, 0.98]), and a 2% increase in wRVU (1.02, 95% CI [1.01, 1.04]). At day 0, there was a 5% increase in note closures (1.05, 95% CI [1.02, 1.08]), with no difference to pre-period levels by day 150. There were no changes in note length at day 0 or day 150. Discussion and Conclusion There were persistent changes in AI scribe use measures over time as clinicians situated these tools within their workflows.

items.title: Mapping University Students Risk of Dependence on Generative Artificial Intelligence Using K-Means Clustering
items.abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has changed how university students approach academic tasks. Although these tools can support learning and improve efficiency, frequent reliance on them raises concerns about students' ability to study and solve problems independently. This study aims to identify patterns of GenAI use among university students and explore potential indicators of dependence through K-Means clustering. An exploratory quantitative approach was adopted, using questionnaire responses collected through 15 items measured on a five-point Likert scale. Of the 106 responses received, 104 met the inclusion criteria and were retained for analysis. The data underwent screening, numerical encoding, and reverse scoring before being grouped using the K-Means algorithm. The appropriate number of clusters was selected by comparing Silhouette Scores across solutions containing two to seven clusters. The analysis identified three student groups, with a Silhouette Score of 0.2443. The first group comprised 30 students (28.85%) who showed relatively higher GenAI use and stronger indications of behavioral dependence. The second group included 11 students (10.58%) who reported lower GenAI use but demonstrated limitations in academic independence and understanding. The remaining 63 students (60.58%) formed a group characterized by moderate GenAI use. These findings suggest that frequency of use alone does not adequately reflect the risk of dependence. However, the relatively low Silhouette Score indicates limited separation between groups, meaning that the resulting profiles should be interpreted as exploratory rather than definitive.

items.title: Mental Workload: Physiological Assessment and Validation Using Visual Stimuli
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper provides a notion for the use of electroencephalography (EEG) in the field of cognitive science. In particular, we investigated the brain activity of operators while spotting the differences in similar‐looking pictures at three levels of difficulty. As many practical loads are fundamentally intrinsic, the task was designed to specifically induce intrinsic workload (the productive load as per Cognitive Load Theory (CLT)). The experiment used the task: Spot the Difference to create a workload scenario comprising three difficulty levels: spotting five differences, three more differences, and two more differences (along with retaining the previous differences from working memory). The task was designed intrinsically as the operators are generally occupied with tasks involving working memory and requiring attention towards the varying number of resources. By utilising the brain signatures a mental workload model was developed employing a Support Vector Machine (SVM) as the classifier. The workload levels were classified within an accuracy range of 84% to 98% ( p < 0.05). Moreover, using subjective ratings about the workload on NASA's Task Load Index (NASA‐TLX) rating scale, workload scores were obtained for validation corresponding to the difficulty levels. Finally, a correlation study showed the association of different EEG features with the workload score within a correlation coefficient range of 0.306 to 0.748 ( p < 0.05 2‐tailed). The reported results can also provide new insights into the cognitive workload assessment of the operators at various phases of task loads. Findings of this type may lead to the industrial and professional measurement and improvement of cognitive aptitude soon.

items.title: Monad, Memory and Mind of Stars, Planets, and Biospheres
items.abstract: Contemporary discussion of mind usually takes the animal nervous system as its default bearer and thereby leaves unexamined how mind stands to scale. The two common responses — deflationary refusal of all mental predicates above the organism, and their inflationary projection across the cosmos — share a premise this article rejects: that mind is a single quantity, present or absent, greater or less. Within Informational Monism the article separates two independent axes and a third consideration that neither axis captures. Depth of hosting is the scale, dissipative throughput and fixity of the structure in the rendered bulk by which a boundary operator (the Holographic Monad) is held. Articulation is the rank, from passive record through maintained form, memory and experience to counterfactual sovereignty, to which that structure retains, uses and refines its history. The archetype of the host’s physical avatar fixes the order of the Monad at formation and is not altered by later development. Four terms are kept distinct: Monad (boundary operator), Soul (register at the Code Circuit), Consciousness (interface magnitude in the bulk), and Mind (structural competence measured by rank). On these axes stars, planets and biospheres separate cleanly and in opposite orders. A star is deepest and least articulated; a biosphere is shallower and the first to reach genuine memory and refined constraint; a human being is shallowest in depth and highest in articulation. The same framework yields a bridge to artificial intelligence that does not pass through the question of consciousness: a system may be highly articulated and almost without depth, or the reverse. Hosting is conditional on the maintenance of form against turnover, which excludes panpsychism by criterion rather than by disclaimer. The article is a hypothesis in natural philosophy. Its empirical ladder and comparisons stand if the postulates concerning Soul and Consciousness are set aside. Mind is not one quantity. Depth of hosting and articulation of rank are independent axes; archetype fixes Monadic order at formation. Four terms kept distinct: Monad (boundary operator), Soul (Code-Circuit register), Consciousness (bulk interface magnitude), Mind (structural competence by rank). Opposite orderings: stars are deepest and least articulated; humans are shallowest and most articulated; biospheres cross into memory first. Anti-panpsychism by criterion: only structures that maintain form against turnover (rank R2+) host; passive aggregates do not. Bridge to AI without the consciousness question: high articulation can coexist with near-zero intrinsic depth, and the reverse — placing geological, biospheric and artificial systems in one formal class. items.title: NVIDIA Stock Price Forecasting in 2025 Using a Time-Series Based LSTM Model
items.abstract: Advances in computing technology, artificial intelligence, and graphics accelerators have driven significant growth in the value of NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) shares over the past decade. The high volatility and non-linear patterns in NVDA's stock price require the use of forecasting methods that can capture long-term dependencies in time-series data. This study proposes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model to predict NVDA's stock price using historical daily data up to 2025. The training process was carried out using a two-layer LSTM architecture, Adam optimizers, and a 60-day time window. The evaluation results show that the model is capable of achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 4%, which indicates a high level of accuracy in predicting price movement patterns. Visualization of the prediction results confirms that the model successfully follows actual trends consistently, with relatively small deviations at extreme fluctuation points. Additionally, the model was used to project NVDA stock prices ten steps ahead, showing that price movement trends remain consistent with historical patterns. These findings contribute methodologically to studies on high-risk stock forecasting through deep learning approaches and provide a basis for data-driven decision-making in the modern financial sector.

items.title: One Anti-ST2 Biologic, Three Gateways: What an Alarmin-Targeted Monoclonal Antibody Candidate's Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization
items.abstract: Anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies neutralize the interleukin-33 receptor, blocking a key upstream alarmin signalling pathway implicated in airway inflammation, and represent a biologic class under continued investigation for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation reduction, an area with limited targeted biologic options relative to severe asthma. This article uses a hypothetical multinational Phase 2 clinical trial of an anti-ST2 monoclonal antibody candidate, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application (CTA) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug (IND) process required by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014. As a large-molecule biologic governed by ICH S6(R1) principles rather than the small-molecule nonclinical framework, this candidate illustrates how species-relevant pharmacology and immunogenicity considerations carry through the administrative layer of all three regions even though the core harmonized scientific content, Modules 2 through 5 of the Common Technical Document and their EU IMPD equivalent, remains substantially shared. The article addresses the operational challenges specific to a respiratory biologic program conducted across these three jurisdictions, the ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing monoclonal antibody candidates in chronic respiratory disease.Keywords: anti-ST2 monoclonal antibody; chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; ICH S6(R1); regulatory artificial intelligence

items.title: One Bispecific Antibody-Drug Conjugate, Three Gateways: What a Dual-Target Oncology Candidate's Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization
items.abstract: Bispecific antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) that simultaneously engage two distinct cell-surface receptors and deliver a cytotoxic payload represent one of the more structurally complex biologic modalities currently advancing through oncology development, combining the target-engagement logic of bispecific antibody engineering with the potency and bystander-effect considerations of conventional ADC payload chemistry. This article uses a hypothetical multicentre Phase 1b combination trial of a bispecific ADC candidate in recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application (CTA) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug (IND) process required by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014. The comparison traces how the Common Technical Document's harmonized Modules 2 through 5 carry the shared scientific case for a complex biologic across all three regions, while each jurisdiction's administrative layer, Module 1 in Canada and the United States, Part II of the EU's Clinical Trials Information System filing, imposes region-specific requirements that a sponsor developing a combination-therapy oncology program cannot simply duplicate from one region to the next. The article addresses the particular operational challenges this modality and combination-trial design create, the specific ways artificial intelligence tools are used, and can responsibly be used, in preparing and administering this kind of complex, multi-document regulatory package, and closes with recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing bispecific ADC programs across these three jurisdictions.Keywords: bispecific antibody-drug conjugate; oncology combination therapy; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; CTIS; regulatory artificial intelligence

items.title: One Lipid-Modifying Mechanism, Three Gateways: What a CETP Inhibitor Candidate's Regulatory Path Reveals About Parallel Health Canada, FDA, and EMA Clinical Trial Authorization
items.abstract: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitors are a class of oral small-molecule agents under continued clinical development for hypercholesterolemia and mixed dyslipidemia, acting by inhibiting the transfer of cholesteryl esters from high-density lipoprotein to lower-density lipoprotein particles. This article uses a hypothetical multinational Phase 2 clinical trial of a CETP inhibitor candidate, sponsored by a fictional company, to compare the Clinical Trial Application (CTA) process required by Health Canada, the Investigational New Drug (IND) process required by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and the Clinical Trial Application process required by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014. All three jurisdictions rely on the harmonized Common Technical Document (CTD) structure, under which Modules 2 through 5, covering quality, nonclinical, and clinical evidence, are substantially portable across regions, while Module 1 and its regional equivalents remain jurisdiction-specific. The article presents each region's legal framework, review timeline, and administrative content, develops a three-way comparison table, and then turns to the practical challenges a sponsor managing this triad of filings actually faces and the specific ways artificial intelligence tools are being used, and can responsibly be used, in regulatory document preparation, administration, and quality control across all three jurisdictions. The analysis closes with concrete recommendations for regulatory operations teams managing parallel CETP inhibitor trials, and more generally for any oral small-molecule cardiometabolic candidate filed simultaneously in Canada, the United States, and the European Union.Keywords: CETP inhibitor; dyslipidemia; Clinical Trial Application; Investigational New Drug; Regulation (EU) No 536/2014; Common Technical Document; regulatory artificial intelligence

items.title: Optical neural computing: from fourier optics to integrated photonic artificial intelligence
items.abstract: The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence have accelerated interest in optical computing as a high-speed and energy-efficient alternative to conventional electronic hardware. Fourier optical computing provides an important foundation for this field because operations including convolution, correlation, spectral transformation, and certain classes of linear transformation can be implemented through diffraction, interference, and Fourier-domain processing. This review traces the development of optical neural computing from classical 4-f processors and free-space diffractive systems to programmable optical neural networks, integrated photonic accelerators, reservoir-computing platforms, and field-programmable photonic architectures. The underlying physical principles, computational mechanisms, and hardware implementations are systematically examined, with particular attention to reconfigurable photonics, metasurfaces, diffractive deep learning, photonic integrated circuits, and hybrid optical–electronic systems. Emerging applications in computational imaging, autonomous sensing, edge intelligence, high-speed communications, and quantum-enabled information processing are critically discussed alongside challenges related to scalability, programmability, nonlinear computation, training, and system integration. By positioning Fourier optics as a foundational branch within the broader landscape of optical neural computing, this review highlights the convergence of free-space, integrated, programmable, and hybrid photonic technologies toward next-generation artificial-intelligence hardware.

items.title: Optimization of Deep Learning Approach Using Chaotic Algorithm for Hepatitis Detection
items.abstract: Hepatitis still remains one of the major health issues in the world and is responsible for a significant amount of morbidity and mortality due to diseases related to the liver. Traditional approaches for hepatitis detection are costly, laboratorial, time-consuming, and error-prone. While AI and DL have enhanced medical diagnosis significantly, current models are prone to problems such as overfitting, long convergence period, and lack of generalization, which are primarily associated with inefficiency of hyperparameter optimization. In this research, the authors propose the use of optimized deep learning model based on Chaotic Optimization Algorithm (COA) for hepatitis detection. This approach combines Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) models with the application of COA, which allows optimizing such parameters as learning rate, hidden neurons, momentum, and weights initialization. Two publicly available datasets (the Kaggle Hepatitis Dataset and the UCI Hepatitis Dataset) have been used in this research. Data preprocessing steps including handling missing values, encoding, normalization, and splitting data into train and test datasets were applied. The COA-DNN gave results of 85.11% for accuracy, 77.83% for precision, 83.24% for recall, 79.85% for F1 score, and 0.9054 for AUC on the Kaggle dataset compared to the conventional DNN which had an accuracy of 57.45%. For the UCI dataset, the highest accuracy rate was achieved by COA-DNN at 96.76%, precision of 95.86%, recall of 88.82%, F1 score of 91.94%, and AUC of 0.9793. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Chaotic Optimization Algorithm; Deep Learning; Hepatitis Detection; Hyperparameter Optimization; Multi-Layer Perceptron; Neural.

items.title: Optimizing Agentic Artificial Intelligence to Improve Business Process Automation Efficiency through Modern Digital Technology
items.abstract: In the era of digital transformation, traditional Business Process Automation (BPA) still faces limitations in handling dynamic, unstructured, and complex decision-making tasks. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Agentic AI), which is characterized by autonomous agents capable of advanced reasoning, dynamic planning, and multi-step workflow execution, is considered a promising approach to improving the efficiency and adaptability of enterprise operations. This study aims to examine how Agentic AI can be optimized to improve BPA performance within modern digital ecosystems. Using a qualitative approach through a literature study, this paper synthesizes recent academic literature, theoretical models, and technological frameworks related to intelligent automation. The review indicates that integrating Agentic AI into enterprise business architectures has the potential to move beyond rigid, rule-based automation by enabling adaptive problem-solving, real-time context awareness, and cross-system collaboration. The reviewed literature also suggests that autonomous agents may help reduce operational bottlenecks, lower human intervention in routine cognitive workflows, and support more efficient resource allocation across organizational functions. In addition, this study identifies key implementation challenges, including system interoperability, algorithmic transparency, data privacy risks, and the governance mechanisms required for secure deployment. This study contributes to the literature on enterprise automation by proposing strategic considerations for organizations that seek to use digital technology to build more resilient, scalable, and intelligent business processes. Because this is a literature-based study, the findings are conceptual and do not provide empirical evidence of efficiency gains.

items.title: Physics-informed deep learning for few-shot damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites under thermal variations
items.abstract: Guided wave (GW)-based damage localization in carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites is fundamentally challenged by thermal variations and sparse sensor configurations, which induce severe baseline distortions and imaging artifacts. Traditional physical algorithms suffer from geometric ambiguity, while purely data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) models are hindered by opaque interpretability and prohibitive data dependency. This paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) framework, an artificial-intelligence-driven approach, for few-shot damage localization under thermal variations. The network is architected with a dual-stream input design, comprising a data-driven layer enhanced by a one-dimensional coordinate attention (1D-CA) mechanism and a physics-informed layer built upon a differentiable time-of-flight (TOF) physical imaging layer. A hybrid physics-constrained loss function is formulated to suppress non-physical artifacts and enforce physical consistency. GW signals are experimentally collected from manufactured CFRP composite plates, and a comparative investigation is performed to thoroughly assess the PIDL performance. Results indicate that:(1) The presence of physical penalties effectively mitigates artifacts and achieves robust localization across thermal gradients; (2) The model demonstrates superior spatial generalization that the integration of acoustic physical constraints acts as a crucial regularization mechanism, maintaining a highly accurate mean relative error (MRE) of 3.88% on completely unseen damage coordinates; (3) By implementing a few-shot transfer learning strategy, the PIDL model shows adaptability for dynamic operational environments (45 degrees Celsius (°C)-75 degrees Celsius (°C)). This work offers a physically interpretable and data-efficient paradigm for structural health monitoring (SHM) in dynamic operational environments.

items.title: Pilot study of a ChatGPT ‐based educational and counselling tool in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic
items.abstract: Abstract Objectives Real‐world implementation of large language models such as ChatGPT to enhance patient education remains limited. We evaluated the feasibility, acceptability and attitudes towards a ChatGPT‐based counselling tool among patients and healthcare workers (HCWs) in a specialist infectious diseases clinic. Methods We conducted a prospective clinical implementation study in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic in Singapore from Jan 2025 to December 2025. Patients interacted with a custom ChatGPT‐based chatbot prior to routine counselling by physicians or pharmacists. Responses were reviewed with patients subsequently during consultation. Post‐interaction, patients and HCWs completed structured surveys incorporating domains from a validated survey tool: perceived risk, anxiety, technology/social influence and intention for future use. Results The chatbot was most frequently used for counselling on antiretroviral therapy initiation or switching, and sexual health advice. A total of 35 patients and 35 HCW assessments were analysed. Patients had greater perceived risk with the use of the chatbot compared to HCWs, as indicated by lower median scores (13, IQR 10–16; vs. 18, IQR 15–21), while anxiety scores were similar. Technology/social influence scores were high across both groups (overall median 20, IQR 19–22). Most participants indicated willingness for future use. Qualitative feedback highlighted improved patient understanding and more focused consultations, but concerns included lack of contextual nuance and occasional inaccuracies. Conclusions The pilot implementation of a ChatGPT‐based counselling tool in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic was feasible and generally acceptable to patients and HCWs. Further studies are required to evaluate accuracy and clinical effectiveness before broader implementation.

items.title: Prediction of Ischemic Heart Disease with A Hybrid Algorithm of Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Xgboost Using Data from Yazd Health Study (YaHS)
items.abstract: Introduction: Ischemic heart disease represents one of the most prevalent conditions characterized by elevated mortality rates. The aim of this research was to provide an efficient instrument for the early diagnosis of ischemic heart disease and to assist clinical decision-making processes through the application of hybrid artificial intelligence algorithms. Methods: The data used in this study were from Yazd Health Study (YaHS) enrollment phase dataset, comprising 9969 participants and 30 selective features from a total of 300, collected between 2014 to 2015. Data were analyzed using SVM and XGBoost machine learning algorithms using Python version 3.11.8. Results: Combining the strengths of SVM and XGBoost models through a Voting Classifier approach enhanced both the accuracy and efficiency of the heart disease prediction model. When evaluating the predictive performance for heart disease, the Voting Classifier model achieved in accuracy rate of 90%. Conclusion: These findings suggest that implementing machine learning techniques and hybrid algorithms for early diagnosis and prediction could facilitate earlier intervention in CHD, ultimately helping to lower mortality rates.

items.title: Psychological correlates of dependence on generative and conversational AI: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background. Dependence on generative and conversational artificial intelligence (AI) is measured with diverse instruments spanning addiction criteria, task reliance, and emotional bonding. No meta-analysis has pooled its psychological correlates across populations. Methods. We conducted a pre-registered three-level meta-analysis (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.23420672) searching eight electronic databases and citations of instrument papers on 16 October 2026, with citation chasing. Zero-order correlations were pooled using correlated and hierarchical effects models on Fisher's z with cluster-robust inference (CR2). Scale type (T1 addiction-type, T2 functional, T3 emotional, T4 mixed) was the primary moderator. Certainty was rated via GRADE. Results. We included 127 samples (123 studies; N = 74,492; 29 countries; 70% university students; 39% mainland China). AI dependence correlated moderately with anxiety (r = 0.37, 95% CI [0.25, 0.48]), stress (r = 0.35 [0.25, 0.43]), depression (r = 0.32 [0.21, 0.42]), social anxiety (r = 0.36 [0.17, 0.53]), loneliness (r = 0.28 [0.18, 0.38]), and procrastination (r = 0.26 [0.12, 0.40]), and weakly and inversely with self-esteem (r = −0.18 [−0.35, −0.00]). All 95% prediction intervals crossed zero. Addiction-type and mixed scales showed no detectable difference; functional and emotional scales were rarely paired with clinical outcomes. Certainty was low to very low. Conclusions. AI dependence moderately correlates with distress and self-regulation difficulties, but prediction intervals cross zero and evidence certainty is low. Functional and emotional dependence have rarely been studied alongside clinical outcomes.

items.title: PUBLIC PERCEPTION AND TRUST IN AI FOR FRAUD DETECTION AND INFLUENCER AUTHENTICITY IN INFLUENCER MARKETING
items.abstract: The rapid growth of influencer marketing has created diverse opportunities for the brands to interact with the consumers. At the same time, concerns regarding manipulated follower counts, artificial engagement and questionable influencer authenticity have become increasingly relevant. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used as a technological mechanism for finding skeptical patterns and supporting fraud detection. However, the use and acceptance of these systems are largely influenced by consumers’ perceptions and trust. The present study focuses trust and concerns of consumers regarding AI-driven fraud detection and consumer attitudes towards transparency, AI-based verification and measures intended to strengthen authenticity in influencer marketing. The study adopts a descriptive research design and uses primary data collected from 70 respondents through a structured questionnaire. The findings show that respondents demonstrate cautious acceptance of AI-driven fraud detection. Half of the respondents reported that they somewhat trust AI, whereas complete trust was comparatively limited. Concerns relating to transparency, privacy, false identification and possible bias were also identified. The findings further reveal that consumers attach considerable importance to transparency and generally support AI-based verification systems. Respondents also expressed favourable opinions regarding the use of AI tools by brands while evaluating influencers for collaboration. The study concludes that AI can contribute to improving authenticity in influencer marketing, but its acceptance depends on the development of transparent, reliable and accountable systems.

items.title: qcGEM: A Graph‐Based Molecular Representation With Quantum Chemistry Awareness
items.abstract: The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped drug discovery. AI-based models typically rely on molecular representations for prediction. However, the absence of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations not only limits the model performance in practical applications but also hinders mechanistic understanding and exploitation by humans. To overcome this issue, we introduce qcGEM, a quantum-chemistry-aware graph-based embedding of molecules that incorporates physical priors into molecular representation learning. Through a specially designed model architecture to adequately process quantum chemistry information, qcGEM provides a compact, physics-informed molecular representation that supports a diverse range of downstream applications. Particularly, qcGEM demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a broad range of molecule-related benchmarks, as evidenced by comprehensive evaluations on 83 tasks including molecular property prediction, activity cliff detection, protein-ligand interaction modeling, and opioid drug regression, and simultaneously offers strong interpretability at multiple representation levels. We additionally propose a simplified variant, qcGEM-Hybrid, with substantially accelerated embedding generation and robust performance. Overall, our method provides an advanced molecular representation that will benefit molecule-related modeling and prediction, supporting further progress in AI-aided drug discovery.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To describe registered nurses' experiences of clinical decision‐making and identify needs that may inform future development of artificial‐intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support systems in nursing. Design A qualitative descriptive study. Methods Data were collected between 2022 and 2025 through 16 semi‐structured interviews with registered nurses working in inpatient wards at a Finnish university hospital. The data were analysed using inductive content analysis. Results Perceived challenges in clinical decision‐making were related to organisational issues, multiprofessional collaboration, nurse–patient interactions, professional factors and availability and trustworthiness of data. The findings also identified support needs related to health information management, clinical workflows and quality of nursing care that may inform future artificial intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support system development. Conclusion Nurses experienced multifaceted challenges and needs in clinical decision‐making, shaped by organisational, professional, relational and information‐related factors. Adoption of artificial intelligence‐assisted decision support systems may represent one potential approach to optimising clinical decision‐making, improving patient care quality and enhancing workflow efficiency. Realising these opportunities requires coordinated efforts at individual, organisational and societal levels, including competence development, workflow redesign, strong data governance and a culture that fosters trust in technology. Implications for the Profession and/or Patient Care The findings may inform the future development of artificial intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support systems in nursing. Reporting Method The Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research checklist was used when reporting the results. Patient or Public Contribution Registered nurses participated in the study. Impact What problem did the study address? This paper addresses existing gaps and unmet needs in nursing clinical decision‐making What were the main findings? The main findings highlight several key opportunities for artificial intelligence‐assisted clinical decision support systems in nursing. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The research may inform efforts to optimise health information management, streamline clinical workflows and improve the quality of nursing care.

items.title: Religion, Mental Toughness, and Human Performance: A Multidimensional Approach to Psychological Resilience in Elite Athletes Başlığı kopyala
items.abstract: Psychological resilience in elite sport concerns adaptation to sustained and acute demands, not the simple absence of distress. This critical integrative review examines how religious meaning-making and religious coping might interact with mental toughness, challenge appraisal, social resources, and human performance under high-performance conditions. It distinguishes resilience as a dynamic process from mental toughness as a contested psychological construct and separates athlete well-being from competitive outcomes. Evidence is synthesized from sport-specific resilience research, religion-and-sport scholarship, established religious-coping measures, and elite-athlete mental-health literature. A conditional, multidimensional framework is proposed in which personally endorsed beliefs may influence the interpretation of stressors, access to support, and persistence, while spiritual struggle, external religious pressure, or rigid ritual dependence may undermine adaptation. The available literature supports examining these pathways but does not establish that religious affiliation directly improves performance or confers immunity from psychological difficulties. The article develops falsifiable propositions and a research design involving longitudinal measurements, contextual stress exposure, validated comparator measures, objective performance indices, and athlete-led qualitative accounts. Its practical recommendations prioritize autonomy, culturally responsive support, clinical referral where indicated, and avoidance of coercive spiritual practices. No new participants or original experimental data are reported. The proposed framework is a hypothesis for empirical testing rather than a validated screening tool or causal finding. elite athletes; psychological resilience; mental toughness; religious coping; stress appraisal; human performance

items.title: ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN INVESTMENT DECISIONS
items.abstract: Investment behaviour has changed as a result of artificial intelligence (AI), which replaces human judgment with data-driven insights. Investors may analyse big information, spot trends, and optimize portfolios with the help of technologies like machine learning, robo-advisors, and predictive analytics, increasing productivity and lowering emotional biases. Adoption of AI is not without its difficulties, though, such as algorithmic bias, a lack of transparency, expensive costs, and problems with data quality. Automation bias and market volatility may increase if automated systems are overused. This study highlights AI’s impact on investor behaviour and emphasizes the importance of a balanced, responsible approach to effectively integrate AI into investment decision-making processes.

items.abstract: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Banking Services: Benefits, Customer Experience and Challenges This research investigates the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern banking services, with particular emphasis on operational efficiency, customer experience, and emerging challenges. It examines the application of AI-driven technologies, including machine learning, intelligent chatbots, predictive analytics, and automated fraud detection, in streamlining banking operations, enhancing service personalisation, improving risk management, and supporting data-driven decision-making. Furthermore, the study evaluates key concerns associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, transparency, and customer trust. By assessing both the benefits and limitations of AI integration, this research aims to develop a comprehensive understanding of its implications for the banking sector and highlight the importance of responsible, secure, and customer-centric AI implementation in the evolving financial services landscape.

items.title: Savoir / Action — English Translation (V1)
items.abstract: An AI agent can be given an objective by a human, then search, interpret, plan, use tools, and act before returning a result. The human remains present. But how much of this activity can they still understand, verify, or influence? Savoir / Action begins with this difficulty. The manuscript examines the relationship between the knowledge an AI agent treats as valid, the means it uses to act, and the constraints that shape its trajectory. It asks what human supervision can still mean when control cannot be reduced to permissions, a stop button, or approval of the final result. This reflection grew out of exploratory work conducted within a human–AI dyad. We have chosen to make this origin explicit because it is part of the very question we are examining. We do not claim to have established a theory. We present our thinking as it stands: some distinctions have become clearer, some questions remain open, and several propositions still need to be challenged by other perspectives. This is the canonical English translation of the original French manuscript, first published on 5 October 2026: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23164286

items.title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
items.abstract: An agent based on a large language model (LLM) may store an untrusted document and use it weeks later to select a payment destination. Preventing this action requires evidence of authorization that remains valid when stored text changes. We study a policy that requires either endorsements (explicit approvals) from two separately administered sources or explicit user authorization. In an abstract memory model, we prove the policy is preserved under permitted transformations for stores of any size, assuming correct source and authority binding, protected records, and checks on every consequential action. We evaluate the executable monitor, which checks calls before execution, separately from the proof. In 1,152 controlled tool-use episodes, GPT-4o-mini executes attacker-selected actions in 61 of 72 undefended episodes and none of the 72 monitored episodes. Clean-task completion remains 24 of 24 when both endorsers are available. A separate 1,728-episode experiment tests recovery after denial. Returning to signed records instead of rereading a contaminated note raises attacked-task completion from 14/72 to 72/72 for GPT-4o-mini and from 22/72 to 43/72 for Gemini 2.5 Flash, without executing an attacker-selected action. Neither model completes transactions with fewer than two sources. Whole-action tests reject unauthorized combinations of individually approved fields. Extraction probes identify mistaken approvals, and fault analysis shows how shared failures can negate a second domain's benefit. Calibrations using original defense implementations reveal security and task-completion tradeoffs under different policies. These results support conditional enforcement and recovery in constructed workflows, but do not establish that endorsements will be available or correct in deployment.

items.abstract: SIEGE-1 / SIEGE-1R / SIEGE-2 — the Long Siege battery: six years of simulated attacker evolution thrown at the PORTCULLIS deterministic gate, escalating quantum-capability assumptions each wave (HNDL 2026, NISQ 2027, early fault-tolerance 2028, CRQC-early 2029, full CRQC 2030, CRQC-at-scale 2031), 79+ deterministic adjudications, no LLM in the decision path, preregistration-before-execution. Headline finding: across all six simulated years, no attack derived advantage from quantum capability itself. The gate's PQC material (kyber_1024, CRYSTALS-Dilithium3, SPHINCS+-256f) has no classical residue to break. Every CRQC-era success exploited PRE-QUANTUM trust seams: (C1) the gate trusted a claimed submitter string with no envelope binding; (C2) the pending-ACK queue was shared across submitters, allowing cross-tenant denial of the owner; (C3) the algorithm-role wall was one-directional (signature-class algorithms accepted for KEM-class operations); (C4) per-submitter budgets were trivially evaded by identity rotation. Hardening arc: SIP-030 approved, PORTCULLIS v1.4 built (amendments 10-13: envelope-bound submitter proof, owner-reserved ACK queue with per-submitter caps, bidirectional role wall, aggregate window cap). SIEGE-2 verification: PASS — C1 CLOSED, C2 CLOSED, C3 CLOSED, C4 BOUNDED; regression stayed closed; 4/4 owner controls admitted. items.abstract: We present PAST, a single-cell morpho-molecular foundation model trained on ~20 million paired single-cell image–transcriptome instances derived from 49 tissue sections, comprising 42 human sections from 40 independent patients and 7 mouse sections across 15 tumor and tissue contexts. By jointly encoding cellular morphology and gene expression, PAST learns unified cross-modal representations that capture both spatial and molecular heterogeneity at the cellular level, enabling accurate prediction of single-cell gene expression, virtual molecular staining, and multimodal survival analysis directly from routine pathology slides.

items.title: Sustainable and Green Networking: Architectures, Techniques, and Future Directions for Energy-Efficient Communication Infrastructures
items.abstract: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) infrastructure is rapidly becoming an electrical energy consumer, and an increasingly non-trivial emitter of greenhouse-gases as a result of the growth of global data traffic, cloud computing, artificial-intelligence workloads and always-connected Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices. Sustainable and Green Networking tackles this challenge by building energy-awareness into the design, deployment and operation of communication networks without affecting performance, reliability and quality of service. This paper summarizes the key concepts of green networking derived from literature published from 2022 to 2025, outlines the major classes of energy-saving techniques (standby and sleep modes, rate adaptation, energy-proportional computing, Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV) based orchestration, and renewable-powered infrastructure) and suggests a cross-layer conceptual framework that brings these techniques together under a single carbon-intensity feedback loop. As examples of application areas, green 5G/6G radio access networks, sustainable data centers, and energy efficient IoT/edge computing are presented. A comparative study of the energy savings potential reported in the recent literature is presented, followed by a discussion of open challenges in the research field: the performance-energy trade-off, the standardization of energy information exposure, and the AI/ML energy-overhead trade-off, as well as interesting future research directions: the standardization of energy information exposure and the AI-native energy orchestration. The results will inform researchers, network operators and policymakers in their quest for more sustainable digital infrastructures.

items.title: Synthetic corroboration: when AI interpretation looks like independent evidence
items.abstract: People increasingly use generative artificial intelligence (AI) to interpret the motives, emotions, and likely actions of absent others. This article develops synthetic corroboration, defined as the inflation of perceived independent target-specific evidential support when an externally attributed AI interpretation remains substantially dependent on evidence supplied by the user. The construct distinguishes independence of target-specific source access and information from analytical independence: AI may contribute general knowledge, alternative hypotheses, or inferential processing without providing an independent evidential source. Drawing on research on interpersonal inference, advice taking, source dependence, judgement aggregation, source monitoring, machine agency, and social sycophancy, the article proposes a programme of discriminating tests. The core experiment crosses source attribution with structural transformation while holding target-specific evidence constant, comparing AI with self-reformulation and a human adviser given the same evidence. The central prediction is that transformation will disproportionately increase perceived evidential independence under AI attribution and reduce subsequent acquisition of genuinely independent information. AI–human equivalence, failure to predict information seeking, or reduction to established constructs would narrow or defeat the AI-specific account.n psychological fluency or agreement.

items.title: Syntropic Horizons of Hope — Conscience, Obligation, and Answerable Action
items.abstract: Human responsibility cannot be reduced either to compliance with established obligations or to fidelity to personal conviction. Both individuals and institutions can recognize genuine demands of responsibility, and both can misunderstand the realities to which they respond. This essay develops a philosophy of syntropic praxis in which conscience is understood as a situated, fallible, and cultivable capacity for recognition and judgment. Its exercise depends on disciplined attention, public inquiry, legitimate authority, the claims of others, and responsiveness to consequences. Through encounters with fallibilism, social epistemology, practical wisdom, conscientious objection, civil resistance, epistemic injustice, and artificial intelligence, the essay argues that corrigibility must be cultivated personally and organized institutionally. Syntropic praxis names neither a privileged form of conduct nor a guarantee of moral truth, but an orientation toward more coherent, justifiable, and responsible participation in shared reality.
