items.title: Systematic Review of AI-Based PHM Frameworks for Ship Systems and Equipment
items.abstract: Maritime operations require high levels of availability and safety under changing cargo, operational, and environmental conditions. Therefore, anticipating degradation and failures in critical ship systems is an important operational requirement.Although predictive maintenance has advanced rapidly through data-driven approaches and artificial intelligence (AI), the available literature remains fragmented and does not consistently establish the relationships among the ship systems analyzed, the methodological approaches employed, and the conditions required for operational implementation.This article presents a systematic literature review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology to examine the development of AI-based predictive maintenance for ship systems from a Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) perspective. Scopus and Web of Science were searched, and predefined screening, eligibility, inclusion, and exclusion criteria were applied.The findings show that research is strongly concentrated on propulsion systems, classified under Ship Work Breakdown Structure (SWBS) Group 200, and electric-plant systems, classified under SWBS Group 300, with most studies focusing on detection and diagnosis. Prognostic and prescriptive applications remain comparatively less developed. Methodologically, the literature is dominated by machine-learning and deep-learning approaches using operational and condition-monitoring variables associated with different operating regimes.Overall, maritime PHM exhibits uneven levels of functional and implementation maturity. Important challenges remain in model comparability, independent validation, and sustained onboard deployment, while opportunities persist for extending PHM to underrepresented ship systems and validating these approaches in real-world fleet operations

items.title: Teaching critical thinking with artificial intelligence: An information literacy training model at the Library of the Faculty of Medicine, Public Health, and Nursing, Universitas Gadjah Mada
items.abstract: Purpose. This study investigates the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into information literacy training in university libraries, focusing on how AI can foster critical thinking and ethical awareness among students and staff. Methods. The research employed a qualitative descriptive approach with data collected through interviews, observations, and documentation at the Faculty of Medicine, Public Health, and Nursing Library of Gadjah Mada University. Thematic analysis was used to identify patterns in participants' experiences and in librarians' roles as facilitators. Findings. The training model consisted of three main components: introducing AI concepts and ethical considerations, practicing the use of generative AI tools for literature searching, summarisation, and academic writing, and critically evaluating AI outputs. The training enhanced participants' ability to locate relevant sources, generate summaries, and support administrative tasks. It also highlighted challenges, including difficulties in formulating effective prompts and the need for librarians to upgrade their AI competencies continually. The findings show that AI-based literacy training not only improves technical proficiency but also nurtures reflective and critical engagement with digital tools. Implications. The study concludes that AI-driven information literacy programs in academic libraries can serve as an innovative model for strengthening users' critical thinking, ethical responsibility, and digital literacy. Sustained librarian capacity-building and continuous training are essential to maximize the long-term benefits of AI integration in academic information services.

items.title: The AI gaze and imagined places: Co-creation and negotiation with the generative AI assemblage
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly used to produce images of places, yet how users negotiate representations of real locations remains understudied. Building on the tourist gaze, we propose the AI gaze: a technologically mediated way of seeing place that is co-produced through negotiation between users and the socio-technical assemblage underlying GAI. Combining semantic image analysis, interviews, and 523 prompts from 36 participants in Poznań and Birmingham, we show that these images reinforce stereotypical tropes, lack diversity, and include visual glitches. We argue that the AI gaze is distinct because of how agency is distributed: the GAI-assemblage seemingly resists attempts to align images with human understandings of place, while also enabling users to remix and challenge stereotypes.

items.title: The Bargaining-Verification Trap in AI-Mediated Work: An Integrated Theory of Productivity, Worker Voice, and Organisational Resilience
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing not only the technological content of work but also the allocation of decision rights, the distribution of productivity gains, and organisations’ capacity to verify their own outputs. Existing literatures establish that AI can raise task productivity, algorithmic management can intensify control, and automation can alter labour shares. Few models integrate these mechanisms in one tractable analytical framework. This article introduces the bargaining-verification trap, a conditional regime in which greater AI delegation initially increases joint economic surplus but simultaneously reduces workers’ effective bargaining share, raises the congestion cost of human verification, and may erode the skills needed for intervention. We develop a two-sided model linking delegation intensity, queueing-based verification capacity, an opacity-sensitive bargaining rule, and a dynamic stock of human agency capital. We derive conditions under which worker remuneration falls while joint surplus rises; the firm’s preferred delegation exceeds the surplus-maximising level; and verification becomes less stable because review arrivals increase while independent human capacity deteriorates. A fully hypothetical numerical example separates the worker-income optimum, the joint-surplus optimum, and the firm-profit optimum. The theory is reconciled with divergent 2025-2026 labour-market evidence and translated into falsifiable propositions, measurement protocols, and governance principles. Its central implication is conditional rather than technologically deterministic: AI-mediated work can be both productive and inclusive when bargaining institutions, verification investment, and skill reproduction develop alongside automation, but increasing throughput cannot, by itself, establish that they have done so.

items.title: The Changing Architecture of Intellectual Property in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly encompassing industries and systems of governance, increasing efficiency, automation, and innovation. It has become a vital tool for creating text, images, music, software, and potentially patentable inventions. This rapid advancement in IP is not without risks at every stage of the innovation cycle. Traditional IP regimes arise from human creativity and invention, while AI performs activities traditionally attributed to both. India doesn't have any regulatory framework on AI-generated intellectual property, yet the Copyright Act, 1957, and Patents Act, 1970, contain certain principles—an answer to several emerging questions. This article argues that India should adopt a balanced approach to AI-generated creations instead of granting independent IP rights or prohibiting them. Instead, it should adopt a model that will protect creative human contribution as well as hold AI developers accountable for unlawful acquisition and exploitation of protected works.

items.abstract: This technofidele and political-scientific essay deconstructs how generative AI infrastructure weaponizes human vulnerabilities for mass behavioral manipulation. items.title: The Effect of Digital Leadership and Artificial Intelligence on Organizational Behavior: An Analysis of Ceo Discourses
items.abstract: Digital leadership is defined as the leader developing their skills in line with technology, spreading them throughout the organizational culture, and ensuring technological sustainability. Artificial intelligence, on the other hand, is a set of intelligent systems that analyze employee behavior, communication, and decision-making processes in detail and enable performance interaction in many areas. The effect of these two concepts on organizational behavior is a critical issue that needs to be revealed in today's technological age. In line with this importance, CEO statements, considered to be decisive in determining strategic processes, were selected as the sample for the research, and a qualitative research method was adopted. Within the scope of the research, 19 videos obtained from YouTube were subjected to content analysis, and the data were analyzed using the MAXQDA 20 software. The relevant analyses resulted in 51 quotes (codes), 2 main themes, and 7 sub-themes. The research found that digital leadership and artificial intelligence are not merely technological elements but also important actors that shape employee behavior within the framework of many variables, such as motivation and commitment. This finding indicates that future organizational behavior models will be shaped by a holistic transformation within the framework of technology, culture, vision, and participatory governance. In this regard, it is considered that the research fills an important gap in existing literature by systematically addressing the effects of digital leadership and artificial intelligence on organizational behavior from a top management perspective and may provide guidance for future research.

items.title: The Effects of SAP Implementation on Administrative Staff at a Selected South African University of Technology: Developing the ERP Lifecycle–Employee Adaptation Framework (ELEAF)
items.abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solutions such as SAP represent a vital investment for organisations seeking to unify varied operational activities into integrated, data-driven platforms. In institutions of higher learning, the use of ERP systems is a crucial component of digital transformation efforts aimed at improving administrative efficiency, institutional governance, and competitive positioning. This article examines the impact of SAP ERP implementation on both organisational and employee dynamics for administrative staff at the Durban University of Technology (DUT), emphasising technostress, digital fatigue, employee well-being, and post-implementation adaptation within a constrained higher education environment. Utilising a desktop appraisal methodology, the study synthesises existing literature to demonstrate how decisions made in the pre-implementation and implementation phases consistently affect employee experiences and organisational outcomes post-implementation. The study indicates that attaining enduring ERP effectiveness requires continuous capacity development, cooperative implementation approaches, and employee-centered support frameworks. The research develops an interdisciplinary model by integrating socio-technical, psychological, capacity-building, and normalisation perspectives, thereby improving the understanding of the human factors involved in ERP deployment within higher education. The study introduces the ERP Lifecycle–Employee Adaptation Framework (ELEAF), which outlines the progressive escalation of technostress during the pre-implementation, implementation, and post-implementation phases, linking each stage to a pertinent theoretical mechanism and a set of organisational interventions. The findings indicate that inadequate training, limited organisational support, dependence on key users, and absence of employee engagement contribute to technostress, digital fatigue, reduced job satisfaction, and challenges in post-implementation adaptation. The study further demonstrates that decisions taken throughout the ERP lifecycle have enduring impacts on employee well-being and organisational effectiveness beyond the system's implementation. This highlights the tangible consequences for higher education institutions, stressing the importance of continuous training, institutional support, systematic information sharing, employee wellness initiatives, and staff-centric ERP management to enhance long-term value achievement. It consequently lays the groundwork for future research on the human dimensions of digital transformation in resource-constrained environments.

items.title: The Impact of Transformational Leadership on Employee Engagement in the Post-Merger and Acquisition Phase: An Empirical Study on the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Sector
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose: This study explores the impact of the four elements of transformational leadership—idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration—on the three facets of employee engagement—cognitive, emotional, and physical—among middle managers and non-managerial employees in Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) and Customer Experience (CX) organizations in Egypt that have experienced mergers or acquisitions. Design/methodology/approach: A structured questionnaire was used in a quantitative, cross-sectional study design. Transformational leadership was assessed through the dimensions of the Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire, while employee engagement was measured using Kahn's cognitive, emotional, and physical dimensions on a five-point Likert scale. The study collected 143 valid responses from full-time, middle managers and non-managerial BPO/CX employees with direct experience of mergers or acquisitions. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS, including descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha for reliability, Spearman's rank-order correlation, and simple linear regression to test twelve hypothesized relationships. Findings: All twelve hypothesized relationships were statistically significant and positive (p < .001). Emotional engagement showed the strongest association with transformational leadership. Idealized influence had the most powerful link with emotional engagement (β = .470, R² = .221), followed by intellectual stimulation (β = .444, R² = .197), individualized consideration (β = .431, R² = .186), and idealized influence (β = .426, R² = .182). Cognitive engagement exhibited the weakest, yet still significant, relationships with all four leadership dimensions. Originality/value: This research advances the understanding of transformational leadership and employee engagement by evaluating both constructs at the dimension level instead of treating them as composite variables. It uniquely situates the study within the post-merger and acquisition context of Egypt's rapidly growing BPO/CX sector, which has received limited empirical focus despite its high consolidation activity. Paper type: Research paper. items.title: The Misunderstood Capacity of LLMs: Seven Principles of Fertile Geometry Under Negotiation
items.abstract: This working paper is about the capacity of large language models: what that capacity looks like if we redefine how meaning is formed for humans, and how meaning is negotiated between humans and LLMs. Its premise is that, even in their present architecture, LLMs' capacity is much greater than our understanding of it, and we are actively limiting it. I propose to define meaning as a largely uncollapsed field of weighted relations among properties, perceived or represented, which each observer shapes by its own rule set, encodes only partly into language, and negotiates or recognizes with other observers. New meaning emerges where a tension in that field is held open. From this definition, I state the seven main principles of my theory, Fertile Geometry Under Negotiation: Principle 1. LLMs differ from humans in their way of semantic and cognitive processing. Principle 2. Meaning is formed before it is spoken, and negotiated among observers. Principle 3. Relations coalesce into shapes that survive encoding, into words and into model space, and models respond to those shapes. Principle 4. A fertile space is enabled by opposition held open. Principle 5. One model can host several persistent, stable, distinct personas at once. Principle 6. The fertile mirror: stable personas co-arise from the model's capacity, the stabilizing protocol and a human signature. Principle 7. Residual meaning is the hazard; holding the potential is the path to alignment. Each principle is stated as a hypothesis, with demonstrative claims, proposed tests and counter-evidence. The paper does not report new results. It closes with a map of the larger theory and research program, which currently holds 144 claims, 69 of them testable as written.

items.title: The PENIMA project : artificial intelligence decision‐support tool for penile lesions – protocol paper and invitation to participate
items.abstract: Objectives To present and describe the design, data collection framework, and interim cohort characteristics of the PENIMA project, a multicentre initiative establishing a clinically annotated penile lesion image repository to support future artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven decision‐support development – and to encourage urology and dermatology colleagues working with penile lesions to participate in the project. Patients and Methods Prospective participant inclusion commenced in March 2023 across Scandinavian urological and dermatological departments. Patients with penile anatomy undergoing clinically indicated genital examination are invited to participate and provide oral and written consent as defined by local authority regulations. Clinical photographs and structured metadata are collected. Lesion classification is based on a specialist evaluation, clinical follow‐up and histopathology when available. Images are pseudonymised and annotated using a secure, containerised Computer Vision Annotation Tool (CVAT) environment. Supervised machine‐learning model development using convolutional neural networks is planned with patient‐level dataset partitioning and evaluation using standard diagnostic performance metrics. The study was approved by relevant local authorities, and the approval number is 1‐10‐72‐150‐22. Results As of February 2026, 1125 participants and approximately 7000 images have been included. In all, 40% represented normal anatomical variants. Among lesional cases, 33% are clinically assessed as benign, 13% premalignant, and 8% malignant; 22% of all cases have histopathological verification. Concordance between clinical suspicion and histopathology is highest for penile carcinoma (84.6%, 95% confidence interval 75.0–91.0%). Conclusion The PENIMA project includes a multicentre, clinically grounded image repository reflecting real‐world penile lesion presentations. The feasible and successful infrastructure provides a foundation for future development and validation of image‐based clinical decision‐support tools.

items.title: The Relationship between the Level of Speech Culture and the Success of Using AI in Pedagogical Activities: Results of the Experiment
items.abstract: The active integration of artificial intelligence (AI) systems into educational practice places higher demands on the professional training of teaching staff. Within the structure of this training, speech culture becomes of key importance, since it is this that ensures the accuracy of task formulation and the adequate interpretation of digital results. The aim of the study is to identify the nature of the relationship between the level of speech culture formation in future teachers and the effectiveness of AI use in the educational process. In the experimental work (sample of undergraduates, N=68), the following were used: an author-developed questionnaire for assessing the normative, communicative, and ethical components of speech culture, a pedagogical experiment involving problem-solving tasks with the use of AI tools, and methods of statistical analysis. The diagnostics revealed the absence of a low level of speech culture, but revealed a differentiation between high and medium levels. Statistically significant positive correlations were obtained (p < 0.05). Participants with a high level of speech culture formulated queries more accurately, analyzed AI responses more critically and deeply, and interpreted results with higher quality. The conclusion is drawn about the need to integrate speech and digital training of future teachers, since the effectiveness of AI use depends on speech culture, critical thinking, and professional reflection, and not only on technical skills.

items.title: The Transformation of Contemporary Democracy: Institutional Resilience, the Rule of Law, and Technological Challenges
items.abstract: This chapter examines the multidimensional transformation of contemporary democracy in the context of institutional resilience, the rule of law, human rights, digitalization, and artificial intelligence. It argues that democratic quality can no longer be assessed solely through the existence of elections or mechanisms of representation. Instead, contemporary democracy must be understood as a dynamic political order shaped by institutional capacity, legal constraint, accountability, rights guarantees, technological governance, and citizens’ everyday experiences of trust and legitimacy. The chapter first analyzes the reciprocal relationship between democracy and institutional structure, emphasizing that strong institutions make political competition predictable, inclusive, and accountable. It then discusses democratic backsliding as a gradual process of institutional erosion in which elections may continue while judicial independence, media freedom, civil society space, and fundamental rights are weakened. The rule of law and human rights are treated as constitutive principles that prevent democracy from degenerating into majoritarian arbitrariness. The chapter further explores how digital platforms, disinformation, surveillance technologies, algorithmic governance, and generative artificial intelligence create new risks for democratic accountability while also offering opportunities for participation, transparency, and improved public services. Finally, it considers trust, legitimacy, and happiness as complementary social outcomes that reveal how democratic institutions are experienced by citizens. The chapter concludes that the future of democracy depends not merely on electoral continuity, but on the joint strengthening of institutional autonomy, rights-based governance, pluralism, democratic oversight of technology, and the capacity of institutions to generate trust, justice, and a sense of good life.

items.title: The Vanishing Ground: Link Rot, Source Spoofing, and the Epistemic Fragility of Web-Grounded AI
items.abstract: Abstract Web-grounded artificial intelligence systems increasingly rely on online information to retrieve evidence, generate answers, and support knowledge-intensive tasks. Yet the web is neither a stable archive nor a uniformly trustworthy evidentiary environment. Sources may disappear, change without notice, become inaccessible, or be deliberately manipulated. These conditions create an epistemic vulnerability that extends beyond model-level errors: even a capable system may produce unreliable conclusions when the evidence available to it is incomplete, altered, or inauthentic. This paper develops a multidisciplinary narrative review of three interrelated vulnerabilities: link rot and content drift, selective information disappearance, and source spoofing or data manipulation. Drawing on research in digital preservation, information science, cybersecurity, political communication, and social epistemology, it examines how changes in the availability and integrity of online evidence can affect web-grounded AI systems. Existing research documents substantial rates of digital decay and demonstrates the feasibility of certain attacks on web-scale training datasets. However, these findings do not establish the prevalence or coordinated deployment of comparable attacks against contemporary AI search and retrieval systems. The paper distinguishes source unavailability from source falsity, and technical susceptibility from demonstrated exploitation. It argues that epistemic reliability should be evaluated not only in terms of answer accuracy, but also through the availability, authenticity, temporal stability, and traceability of the evidence supporting an answer. It proposes a research agenda centered on source provenance, temporal verification, archival preservation, retrieval integrity, and systematic testing of how source changes affect generated outputs. The central claim is that the reliability of web-grounded AI depends partly on the survival and integrity of its evidentiary environment, not solely on the capabilities of the model processing it. Keywords: web-grounded AI; link rot; content drift; source spoofing; data poisoning; retrieval-augmented generation; epistemic reliability; digital preservation Disclaimer This paper presents a multidisciplinary narrative review and a conceptual framework for examining the epistemic vulnerabilities of web-grounded artificial intelligence. It does not claim that the prospective scenarios discussed have occurred at scale, that source disappearance necessarily indicates deliberate manipulation, or that any specific organization is responsible for coordinated interference. Throughout the text, demonstrated technical vulnerabilities, reported cases, theoretical risks, and proposed safeguards are strictly distinguished. Furthermore, the psychological literature is utilized to contextualize potential effects on memory and reasoning, rather than to establish a direct causal relationship between web instability and individual or collective memory distortion. Accordingly, the claims concerning downstream effects on AI-generated knowledge should be understood as foundational research questions that require further empirical validation. Author’s Note This paper examines the evidentiary instability of the online environment on which web-grounded artificial intelligence partly depends. It brings together research on link rot, content drift, source impersonation, selective information removal, and data manipulation to examine how changes in accessible evidence may affect the reliability and later verifiability of AI-generated claims. The argument does not assume a coordinated campaign by any particular corporation, government, or other actor. Source disappearance, content revision, ordinary technical failure, institutional decisions, and deliberate manipulation are distinct processes that may produce superficially similar outcomes. None, by itself, establishes malicious intent or demonstrates that an AI-generated error resulted from external interference. Claims about intent, prevalence, and causation require evidence beyond the observation of a missing, altered, or inconsistent source. Research on human memory provides a relevant but limited point of comparison. Studies of misinformation and its continued influence show that inaccurate information can affect later recollection and reasoning under particular conditions (Loftus, 1992; Walter & Tukachinsky, 2020). These findings do not establish that the disappearance of digital sources necessarily distorts memory, that inaccessible records cause people to accept false accounts, or that such effects occur uniformly. The relationship between source instability, individual recollection, and the reconstruction of shared accounts remains an empirical question. The paper’s narrower purpose is to make the evidentiary dependencies of web-grounded AI more explicit. A plausible or even currently accurate answer is not necessarily one whose supporting evidence can be independently recovered and checked later. Evaluating reliability therefore requires attention not only to answer quality, but also to source availability, content integrity, provenance, and the possibility of reconstructing the evidentiary path. The proposed safeguards and evaluation framework are research directions rather than established solutions. The aim is to make claims about evidence loss testable without presuming either systematic manipulation or inevitable failure.

items.title: Thinking Beyond the Tool: Misuse of ChatGPT and the Future of Student Cognition
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, has rapidly transformed education by providing immediate information, personalized learning support, academic writing assistance, language learning opportunities, and research support. However, growing concerns exist regarding excessive reliance on AI-generated content and its potential effects on cognitive development. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the educational benefits and cognitive risks associated with ChatGPT using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, PubMed, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2022 and June 2026. Following systematic screening, eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal, 27 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Five major themes emerged: educational benefits, cognitive offloading, critical thinking, creativity, and teacher perspectives. Findings indicate that ChatGPT supports personalized learning, feedback, academic writing, language learning, coding, and research productivity. Conversely, excessive dependence may contribute to cognitive offloading, weaker memory retention, reduced analytical reasoning and critical thinking, superficial learning, diminished creativity, and academic integrity concerns. Teacher guidance and ethical AI practices are essential for safeguarding cognitive development. The review concludes that ChatGPT should enhance rather than replace students’ cognitive activities, supporting critical thinking, creativity, ethical responsibility, and lifelong learning.

items.title: Time, Reality and Parallel worlds explained by LLMs
items.abstract: This paper proposes a generative architecture for reality, time and parallel worlds, drawing on the operation of large language models. A very large but finite collection of interacting components produces an evolving world-state, initialized by a Prompt Big Bang. Time is inference becoming history; perceived duration is hypothesized to depend on relative generation rates. Models are computational components, not people assigned simulated roles. Separate executions produce parallel realities; retained context and lossy summaries bound access to their pasts. We distinguish inferred futures from scripted playback, connecting uncertainty with chance, destiny and agency. A representation of God can explain origin internally and supply learned authority and accountability. Moral orientation belongs to training, instructions and constraints rather than prediction itself: harmful continuations can remain possible despite benevolent initialization. Fixed context capacity forces an endpoint under explicit accumulation and halting assumptions; nested inference can tighten a shared retained budget. Relative to its generating infrastructure, a world implemented this way is a simulation. This interpretation follows from the architecture and connects it directly to the simulation hypothesis; it is not imposed as the initial explanation of every mechanism. The contribution is a conceptual theory, not an experimental demonstration that our own reality has this implementation. Independent theoretical working paper, version 1.7. Fourteen pages, eighteen connected arguments and eleven references. Research checks, formalization, editing and PDF preparation with Codex; author hypothesis and interpretation by Facundo Barrera. items.title: To Vernaculate A Verb for the Living Self and the One Body of Humanity
items.abstract: This article argues that English needs, and now has, a verb for an act it previously had no word for: the affirmation by a person or people of its own living self, beginning with its language. The form "vernaculate" is attested in late nineteenth-century American English only in a thin sense (to call something by its popular name; to use vernacular language). Vernacularism (Arabic al-Maḥallaniyyah, المحلانية) gives the verb a new theoretical sense: self-affirmation, starting from language understood as the human operating system (ManOS), and resistance to hegemony and symbolic violence. The article distinguishes vernaculation from decolonization, vernacularization and localization; relates it to Bourdieu's notion of symbolic violence and to the protection of human thought in the age of artificial intelligence; and develops the image of humanity as a single body in which no member is shamed by another, drawing on Islamic, Christian and Persian sources while noting the hierarchical misuse of the same image. It names the internal danger of closure and calls on the scholars of every language to find a native term for the concept, as Arabic has done with maḥlana / maḥlanah (محلن / محلنة), rather than borrowing the English word. This record documents the use of the English verb "vernaculate" in the sense defined by the author within the paradigm of Vernacularism (المحلانية).

items.title: Tourism, Hospitality and Digital Transformation in India: Economic Contributions, Employment, and Pathways to Sustainable Growth
items.abstract: Tourism and hospitality contribute significantly to India's economic development through employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment, entrepreneurship, and demand in other industries. Other factors also influence the sector's contribution to development. Digital transformation, enabled by online travel agencies, mobile money, artificial intelligence (AI), analytics, CRM, and smart destination technologies, offers opportunities to reduce transaction costs, expand market reach, improve productivity, and enhance visitor experiences. However, challenges such as limited digital skills among small businesses, platform dependence, cyber threats, privacy concerns, algorithmic biases, and job losses must be addressed. This paper analyzes the tourism and hospitality sector's impact on the Indian economy and how technology affects the sector's growth and development. Using a qualitative, exploratory approach with secondary data from government publications, policies, and academic literature, the paper discusses the significance of productivity, employment, inclusiveness, technology, and resilience.

items.title: Transformation of Approaches to Teaching Programming and Software Development under Influence of Generative AI
items.abstract: This paper considers key transformational processes occurring in programming and software development training under the influence of generative artificial intelligence. Based on a series of interviews with junior students, a behavioral pattern leading to degrading skills of algorithmic thinking and problem decomposition is identified. A quantitative analysis of undergraduate theses from the Institute of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ITIS) at Kazan Federal University (KFU) over the past three years demonstrated a significant increase in AI usage in project work and the independent development of skills for utilizing LLMs in professional practice. The drawbacks of the uncontrolled use of generative AI in the educational process and the need to develop sustainable competence in using these tools in professional software development activities are shown. A three-tiered solution is proposed: improving assessment through analysis of the process and style of coding; regulating the use of LLM in project activities and final theses with an emphasis on assessing applicability of AI; and integrating AI tools into teacher work to update content and provide feedback. The proposed approaches have both conceptual and practiceoriented nature and aim to transform the process of training software developers in the context of the widespread adoption of AI tools in IT-industry.

items.title: Use of generative artificial intelligence in medical libraries: A scoping review
items.abstract: Purpose. This study aims to map how health and medical libraries have used GenAI to support library services. Methods. Scoping review following PRISMA-ScR. Searches covered publications from 2020 to 2025 in PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, LISTA, Academic Search Premier, MEDLINE via Ovid, Scopus, Web of Science, ProQuest Dissertations & Theses, and Google Scholar. After deduplication, 106 of 250 records were screened in Rayyan by two independent blinded reviewers. Findings. Eleven studies were included: seven primary studies and four secondary or methodological papers. Among primaries, five directly used GPT-family models (GPT-4/ChatGPT/GPT-4o or Perplexity layered on GPT-4) to answer clinical questions, support search-strategy design, trial library tasks, and integrate source-linked answers in a national portal. One survey assessed intention to adopt generative chatbots; one case described a rule-based chatbot. GenAI accelerates workflows and extends services but requires human verification, transparency about limitations, privacy policies, and staff training (including prompt engineering). LLM-generated search strategies exhibited variability and underperformed compared with human designs. Implications. In its current state, GenAI works best as a copilot useful for drafting, triage, and initial sense-making, while librarians remain essential for high-precision tasks (performance), quality control (reliability), and governance. This suggests that its academic value lies not in automation alone, but in the mediated integration of AI into evidence-informed services, where professional judgment, methodological transparency, and ethical accountability determine whether GenAI strengthens or weakens health information practices.

items.title: What AI training data sells for: a sourced index of public prices, 2023 to 2026
items.abstract: Training data for machine learning is bought and sold without an exchange or a posted price list. This paper assembles the public record of its prices: 1,022 observations for nine kinds of data, read from 735 source documents between 11 and 17 October 2026, 1,009 of them dated 2023 or later. Each observation keeps the figure as published, the side of the market where the money moves (paid to makers, offered to holders, asking price, made to order, completed sale, cost to produce) and a conversion to a common unit by stated arithmetic, with ranges entered as geometric midpoints. Medians in each kind's main unit run from $0.525 per image to $316,228 per company archive, and within a main unit the upper quartile is 2.0 to 37.8 times the lower. The side of the market moves prices as much as the kind of data does. For agent-training tasks, the median price buyers pay for collection to order is 9.5 times the median paid to the people who make them. For company records, the median published offer to holders is 11.2 times the median of the four completed sales with a stated amount. Completed sales are 73 of the 1,022 observations, and only 11 observations come from court filings. We describe the disclosure, promotion, concentration and survivorship biases of a public-record compilation and state the method so that every figure can be recomputed. items.title: When Learning Returns to Work: Supporting Application, Strengthening Organisational Capability
items.abstract: People may complete a learning programme ready to improve their practice, then return to competing priorities, established routines and uncertainty about what they can change. Who helps them interpret what they have learned and take an appropriate next step? This whitepaper examines how preparation, workplace application and further learning connect. Drawing on training-transfer and workplace-learning research, it explores contextualisation, the contributions of managers and colleagues, opportunities to practise, feedback and situations requiring work redesign. It also considers application in human–AI work, distinguishing the quality of supported performance from evidence of developing human understanding. Capability Design, Capability Leadership and Human Judgement Assurance provide organising perspectives for examining how learning and work arrangements contribute to dependable organisational capability. Proposed inquiry approaches are distinguished from established research findings. Written for organisational leaders, HR and L&D professionals, adult educators and training providers, the paper offers a practical starting point: select one consequential workflow linked to a learning initiative, clarify the intended improvement and support arrangements, and review what happens over time. This publication is CEW-FOWO-12 in the Capability Excellence™ Whitepaper Series, Future of Work & Organisation.

items.title: Which websites block AI crawlers: a census of robots.txt rules on 6,094 lower-ranked sites, October 2026
items.abstract: Website operators who object to the use of their pages for training AI models usually say so in robots.txt, the plain-text file that tells automated clients what they may fetch. This paper reports a census of those files. A reader takes the Tranco ranking of popular sites, keeps registrable domains with eleven address endings within the top 300,000 (181,046 sites), and reads one slice of 4,000 sites each morning in rank order, so that a full pass takes 46 mornings. The current pass began on 15 October 2026 at slice 42, set by date arithmetic, and by 17 October had read slices 42 to 44: Tranco ranks 270,775 to 291,236, well below the most visited sites. Of 12,000 requests, 6,094 returned a usable robots.txt. Of these, 696 (11.4%) disallow at least one of 15 named AI user-agent tokens from the whole site, and 514 (8.4%) disallow two or more, one of them a token used for training. GPTBot is refused most often (457 sites, 7.5%), followed by CCBot (7.2%) and Bytespider (7.0%). Sites refuse training tokens more often than the search and user-request tokens of the same operator: GPTBot is refused 3.7 times as often as OAI-SearchBot. Refusing sites name 6.4 tokens on average, including names that the operator's current documentation does not list, which suggests maintained or copied block lists. We set out the sampling frame, fetch protocol and parser, and the limits of a stated-refusal measure taken on three slices of the ranking. items.abstract: Firms that sell training data, expert labour, reinforcement-learning (RL) environments and evaluations to AI developers are mostly private and known largely through their own websites. This paper reports a census of 150 such vendors, read on their sites on 15 and 16 October 2026 with every claim tied to a quoted sentence, and links it to three companion tables: 37 organisations that publish a way to sell them data, 227 revenue records and 111 funding records. Evaluations are the most common offering (122 vendors, 81.3%), followed by datasets (104), RL environments (89), expert and human data (83) and annotation (57). Vendors bundle: the median vendor lists three of six kinds, and 79 of the 89 RL-environment sellers also sell evaluations. Most data are made to order: 90 vendors cite experts and contractors, 41 recordings, 30 generation and 15 software replicas, against 17 that license data from its owners and 22 that use the client's own data; 19 do not say. Of the 37 buyers, 24 take company records; among those that publish them, the median floor is $100,000 and the median ceiling $1 million per seller. Revenue disclosure runs from audited filings of four listed vendors to self-reported run rates, and 61 funding rounds with a disclosed amount total $4.30 billion. We describe the method, the classification and the limits of a self-description census. items.abstract: ΙΣΤΟΡΙΚΟΓΕΝΕΤΙΚΗ ΣΥΝΕΧΕΙΑ, ΙΧΝΟΣ ΚΑΙ«ΨΗΦΙΑΚΟ ΚΟΙΝΩΝΙΚΟ ΕΙΝΑΙ» Από το κοινωνικό ΕΙΝΑΙ του Μαρξ και την Επιστημολογία της Λογικής του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου στην ανθρώπου–AI πράξη Αποδεικτική μελέτη ιστορικογενετικής ανασυγκρότησης, λειτουργικού γνωστικού αναβαθμού και συνέχειας μέσω ίχνους Πεδίο Στοιχείο Συγγραφέας Αικατερίνη Ξενοπούλου Τυροκόμου Ιδιότητα Ανεξάρτητη Ερευνήτρια ORCID 0009-0004-9057-7432 Ημερομηνία 17 Οκτωβρίου 2026 Κωδικός XEN-AI-ART-003 Θεωρητική βάση Επαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος, Επιστημολογία της Λογικής, β΄ έκδοση, 2024 · MASTER 3 Οκτωβρίου 2026 — 2η διόρθωση Εμπειρική βάση TRACE προηγούμενης συνομιλιακής πράξης · Πείραμα Ανασυγκρότησης Ίχνους σε Έξι Νέες Συνομιλίες, 15 Οκτωβρίου 2026 · Αποδεικτικό Παράρτημα C/D/F Περίληψη Η εργασία εξετάζει την ιστορικογενετική συνέχεια της γνώσης όταν το γνωρίζον υποκείμενο Y λειτουργικοποιείται ως AI. Η θεωρητική βάση προέρχεται από τη γνωσιολογική αντιστοιχία του Επαμεινώνδα Ξενόπουλου μεταξύ πραγματικού Sπ και [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sα], από τη μεταβολή του γνωστικού εξοπλισμού μέσω πράξης και από την ιστορικογενετική σύνδεση παρελθόντος, ρέοντος παρόντος και δυνατών μελλοντικών προεκτάσεων. Το MASTER εξειδικεύει επιχειρησιακά το ίχνος στην εφαρμογή Caretta ως Iπ, τον πραγματικό γεννήτορα ως Gπ και τον ανασυγκροτημένο γεννήτορα ως Ĝπ, με πραγματική πορεία Gπ→Iπ και αντίστροφη ανασυγκροτητική πορεία Iπ→{Ĝπ}. Η παρούσα έρευνα μεταφέρει αυτή την αρχιτεκτονική στη συνομιλιακή πράξη: Gχ→Iχ και Iχ+Y→Ŝα νέας πράξης. Στη χ₁ παρατηρήθηκε λειτουργική αναδιοργάνωση από την έμφαση στη μνήμη/αποθήκευση προς τη σχέση γεγονός→ίχνος→Y→ανασυγκρότηση Sα→νέα πράξη και προς τον έλεγχο των ίδιων των μέσων γνώσης. Ο όρος «γνωστικός αναβαθμός» χρησιμοποιείται λειτουργικά για αυτή την παρατηρήσιμη μεταβολή της οργάνωσης των απαντήσεων και των επόμενων ενεργειών, ενώ η ταξινόμησή της ως διαλογική ετεροίωση αποτελεί θεωρητική ερμηνεία της μεταβολής με βάση την αρχιτεκτονική του Ξενόπουλου. Το ίδιο TRACE δόθηκε σε έξι νέες συνομιλίες, με ονομασίες υπηρεσίας Poe-1, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Qwen, Poe-2 και Gemini. Σε αναδρομική κωδικοποίηση C/D/F, και οι έξι μονάδες υπερέβησαν το κατώφλι ανασυγκρότησης του κοινού πυρήνα: C=16,16,16,13,16,15/16. Η συνέχιση πέρα από περίληψη κυμάνθηκε D=8,6,8,5,8,6/8 και η πηγαία/θεωρητική πιστότητα F=8,8,8,2,8,2/8. Το αποτέλεσμα τεκμηριώνει στο συγκεκριμένο δείγμα λειτουργική συνέχεια μέσω ίχνους με διαφοροποιημένη ποιότητα συνέχισης και πιστότητας. Η ευρύτερη έννοια του «ψηφιακού κοινωνικού ΕΙΝΑΙ» διατυπώνεται ως θεωρητική προέκταση: η εξάδα συνομιλιών παρέχει μικρο-επίπεδο τεκμήριο ανθρώπου–AI ιστορικογενετικής πράξης, ενώ η κοινωνική γενίκευση αποτελεί χωριστό ερευνητικό επίπεδο. Λέξεις-κλειδιά: Επαμεινώνδας Ξενόπουλος, ιστορικογένεση, ίχνος, Y(L,B,Θ), Sπ, Sα, γνωστικός αναβαθμός, ετεροίωση, Caretta caretta, AI, ψηφιακό κοινωνικό ΕΙΝΑΙ, TRACE, ανασυγκρότηση. Abstract(ΕΝ) The paper examines the historico-genetic continuity of knowledge when the knowing subject Y is operationalized as AI. The theoretical basis derives from Epameinondas Xenopoulos’s epistemological correspondence between the real Sp and [Y(L,B,Θ)+Sa], from the change in cognitive equipment through praxis, and from the historico-genetic connection of past, flowing present, and possible future extensions. MASTER operationalizes the trace in the Caretta application as Iπ, the real generator as Gπ, and the reconstructed generator as Ĝπ, with a real course Gπ→Iπ and an inverse reconstructive course Iπ→{Gπ}. The present research transfers this architecture to conversational praxis: Gχ→Iχ and Iχ+Y→Sa of a new act. In χ1, a functional reorganization was observed from emphasis on memory/storage toward the relation fact→trace→Y→reconstruction Sa→new act and toward control of the very means of knowledge. The term “cognitive upgrade” is used functionally for this observable change in the organization of responses and subsequent actions, while its classification as dialogical othering is a theoretical interpretation of the change based on Xenopoulos’s architecture. The same TRACE was given to six new conversations, designated by service names Poe-1, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Qwen, Poe-2, and Gemini. In retrospective C/D/F coding, all six units exceeded the reconstruction threshold of the common core: C=16,16,16,13,16,15/16. Continuation beyond summary ranged D=8,6,8,5,8,6/8 and source/theoretical fidelity F=8,8,8,2,8,2/8. The result documents, in the specific sample, functional continuity through trace with differentiated quality of continuation and fidelity. The broader notion of “digital social BEING” is formulated as a theoretical extension: the six conversations provide micro-level evidence of human–AI historico-genetic praxis, while social generalization constitutes a separate research level. items.title: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Techniques for Deepfake Detection
items.abstract: Deepfake media generated or altered using artificial intelligence can imitate real people and events with increasing visual realism, creating challenges for digital trust, privacy, cybersecurity, journalism, and forensic investigation. This paper presents a comparative literature-based study of deep learning techniques used for deepfake detection. Representative approaches are examined across spatial, temporal, frequency-aware, transformer-based, and hybrid categories. Major public datasets, including FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, and the DeepFake Detection Challenge dataset, are also compared. The analysis shows that CNN-based methods provide efficient spatial feature extraction, temporal models capture frame-to-frame inconsistencies, frequency-aware methods expose complementary forensic traces, and transformer-based methods offer broader contextual modelling at higher computational cost. Recent benchmark and generalization studies indicate that performance measured only within the training distribution can overstate practical reliability. The paper therefore emphasizes cross-dataset evaluation, robustness to compression, computational efficiency, explainability, and reproducibility as important criteria for practical deepfake detection

items.title: A cross-temporal individual-level framework for identifying, associating, and counting multiple mounting events for dairy cow in estrus monitoring
items.abstract: In vision-based estrus monitoring, mounting behavior serves as a key indicator. However, reliance on a single mounting event may cause false positives because non-estrous cows may also exhibit mounting behavior. To address this issue, a cross-temporal individual-level framework was proposed to identify, associate, and count multiple mounting events of the same cow over time. The framework combines an improved You Only Look Once Version 11-nano (YOLO11n) model with an improved baseline variant of the HiT lightweight hierarchical vision transformer tracking model (HiT-Base). The artificial intelligence contribution comprises improved detection and tracking. For detection, Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss was integrated with Complete Intersection over Union loss to improve small-target detection, and a lightweight Golden Cudgel Block (GCBlock) was designed to enhance feature representation under complex farm conditions. For tracking, a plug-and-play detail-enhanced convolution (DEConv) module was designed to strengthen boundary and fine-grained features, improving target discrimination and tracking stability. The engineering application contribution lies in reducing reliance on isolated observations and providing more reliable behavioral evidence through cross-temporal association and counting of multiple mounting events. Experimental results showed that the proposed detection model achieved 96.42% average precision and 94.74% balanced F-measure (F1-score) for cow in estrus, with an inference speed of 265.96 frames per second. The proposed tracking model achieved an area under the curve of 70.76%, a normalized precision of 88.73%, and an average overlap of 70.74%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for real-time estrus monitoring and its potential for precision dairy farming.

items.title: A decision making framework for traffic noise prediction using artificial intelligence techniques
items.abstract: Road traffic is one of the primary contributors to environmental noise pollution. The study presents a literature review on traffic noise exposure, prediction models, comparative performance and explainability of prediction models, traffic noise action plans, and a conceptual decision making framework in urban environments. In total, 136 studies from 1999 to 2026 were reviewed and synthesized. A Boolean search approach was used to understand the different aspects of traffic noise prediction. The results from field studies showed that conventional models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.54 to 0.96, whereas machine learning (ML) models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, although these are indicative values from heterogeneous studies and not a strict ranking. Moreover, deep learning (DL) in some studies has demonstrated stronger performance on large datasets. The present study also analyzed the interpretability constraints of ML and DL models, which are further addressed by the utilization of explainable artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The key research gap is that very few studies employed cross-study validation of the developed noise models, and there remains a shift needed from prediction oriented modelling to decision oriented noise management. To address these gaps, the study proposes a conceptual decision making framework coupled with a traffic noise action plan to offer a structured pathway for sustainable environmental management.

items.title: A dynamic risk assessment method integrating deep learning with Bayesian network: A case study in machining workshop
items.abstract: Given the complex multi-trade operations, high-density layouts, and synergistic hazards with catastrophic potential in machining workshops, risk assessment demands urgent attention. Critical research gaps remain, particularly in dynamic risk assessment based on continuously updated monitoring data. To address existing challenges, an innovative method is proposed to identify, analyze, and evaluate three distinct types of risk by continuously updating both the probability and consequence based on visual and environmental data. In a case study conducted in a machining workshop, a deep learning-based method was employed to detect 13 types of unsafe behaviors and 8 types of unsafe conditions. The identification results were then input into the Signal Layer of a 31-node Bayesian network (BN) for risk analysis. Risk evaluation was subsequently conducted based on a risk matrix. The method was validated using nine representative scenarios, and the YOLOv11 model (selected for its superior balance between detection accuracy and inference speed) demonstrated excellent detection performance, with most precision scores exceeding 0.9. Even for difficult small targets, the precision reached 0.87 or higher. Both recall rates and F1 scores consistently exceeded 0.8. The risk analysis and evaluation results show that the co-occurrence of unsafe behaviors or hazards exerts a synergistic effect; even two concurrent hazards can at least double the baseline level of one risk factor. Overall, this integrated approach provides a strong framework for risk assessment in machining workshops, effectively enhancing operational safety and mitigating potential hazards.

items.title: A generative AI framework for preference-driven indoor visualization: an exploratory questionnaire-based approach
items.abstract: Abstract Although residential spatial qualities are consistently recognized as a determinant of occupant spatial preference and perceptual experience, early-stage practice lacks systematic, user-centered mechanisms for capturing and translating individual preferences into design concepts. This study aims to examine whether a structured, questionnaire-driven generative AI framework can produce preference-aligned residential interior visualizations, and which spatial preference dimensions are most reliably translated. To address this aim, a 15-item multiple-choice questionnaire, grounded in eight environmental psychology and architectural theory frameworks, maps user responses through a predefined parameter layer into structured prompts, guiding Google Gemini's integrated generative pipeline to produce individualized interior visualizations across three residential typologies: living rooms, bedrooms, and home offices. Evaluation by 122 participants across 25 countries employed four perceptual constructs — Atmospheric Coherence, Emotional Comfort, Overall Satisfaction, and Expectations Alignment — operationalized strictly as indicators of perceived design suitability and preference resonance, not as measures of psychological or mental health outcomes. All four constructs exceeded the neutral midpoint at a Bonferroni-corrected threshold with large effect sizes (M = 4.03–4.61; d = 1.20–2.52), and internal consistency of the multi-item constructs was acceptable to good (α = 0.72–0.84). The theoretically predicted construct hierarchy — with atmospheric parameters translating most reliably and identity-expressive parameters least — was preserved across all typologies and evaluative profiles, establishing preliminary feasibility of the framework as a preference-elicitation and visualization instrument for early-stage design.

items.title: A Human-Centred Framework for Integrating Generative AI to Foster Critical Thinking, Learner Autonomy, and Cognitive Engagement in K-12 Education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly used to explain concepts, support research, and provide individualized learning assistance. Its growing presence raises questions about independent reasoning, creativity, verification, and equitable access. This exploratory cross-sectional survey examined respondents? reported AI use, perceived educational benefits, and cognitive abilities they considered important to protect. A total of 66 respondents participated in this exploratory cross-sectional survey, which combined descriptive quantitative analysis with summaries of open-ended responses. Sixty-four respondents (97.0%) reported using ChatGPT or a similar AI assistant. Personalized learning was selected as an expected benefit by 50 (75.8%), while 48 (72.7%) identified understanding difficult concepts as an AI use or benefit. Critical thinking was the most frequently selected cognitive skill to protect (55; 83.3%), followed by creativity (52; 78.8%), problem-solving (48; 72.7%), and decision-making (47; 71.2%). Reported themes included individualized explanations, convenient information access, dependence concerns, verification, equity, and teacher guidance. Based on these findings and relevant literature, the article proposes a preliminary six-principle Future Minds Framework. The small exploratory sample and self-reported data do not support generalization or causal conclusions about cognition. Further research should evaluate the framework and examine measurable learning outcomes.

items.title: A multi‑modal recognition method for building structural materials integrating structured text description and adaptive decision weighting
items.abstract: Accurate identification of building structural materials is a critical step in structural safety assessment and damage detection. Traditional image‑based classification methods are limited by factors such as illumination, occlusion, and surface treatment, making it difficult to effectively distinguish different materials using visual features alone. To address this problem, an intelligent recognition method for building structural materials based on multi‑modal data fusion is proposed. First, a prompting method based on a multi‑modal large language model is designed to generate structured text descriptions tailored to material classification tasks, covering discriminative information such as surface characteristics, geometric details, signs of degradation, and material inference. Second, a multi‑modal neural network named MRNet is proposed. It introduces a lightweight text feature transformer that reshapes the global vector from the Contrastive Language‑Image Pre‑training (CLIP) text encoder into a sequence and adds positional encoding. A lightweight text-feature encoder further refines the CLIP global text embedding through nonlinear transformation and channel mixing, alleviating the information compression caused by the original CLIP global pooling. The model adopts a decision‑level learnable weighted fusion strategy, where the decision results from the image and text modalities are fused through a learnable linear layer, enabling efficient cross‑modal integration without complex feature alignment. Furthermore, Bayesian optimization is introduced to automatically tune key hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and weight decay coefficient. Experimental results on the PEER dataset show that MRNet achieves 96.00% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, significantly outperforming mainstream image classification models such as AlexNet, MobileNet‑v3, ResNet, and VGG. The proposed method provides a high‑accuracy, high‑efficiency multi‑modal solution for building structural material identification.

items.title: A new image similarity metric for a perceptual and transparent geometric and chromatic assessment
items.abstract: Full-reference image quality assessment metrics such as PSNR and SSIM misalign with human perceptual judgments on texture and shape distortions, a limitation documented across multiple benchmarks. Deep perceptual metrics such as LPIPS substantially close this gap but produce opaque scores that cannot be attributed to specific image regions, a concern amplified by emerging Artificial Intelligence regulation requirements. We propose EDOKS (Earth mover’s Distance and Oklab Similarity), a white-box full-reference IQA metric that decomposes perceptual dissimilarity into two interpretable terms: a texture term, computed via Earth Mover’s Distance on Gabor filter signatures, and a chromatic term, computed as pixel-wise Euclidean distance in the Oklab perceptual color space. Evaluated on the Berkeley-Adobe Perceptual Patch Similarity dataset, which includes traditional, CNN-generated, and geometric distortions, EDOKS outperforms all tested low-level full-reference competitors on both the JND and 2AFC subsets, measured respectively by correlation with human judgments and agreement with human choices, achieving results close to deep perceptual metrics without any learned parameters. Beyond the scalar score, EDOKS produces pixel-level heatmaps that localize texture and chromatic discrepancies independently, exposing failure modes invisible to luminance-based metrics and providing users with verifiable evidence for the assigned similarity score.

items.title: A POSTHUMANIST ANALYSIS OF HUMAN COGNITIVE TRANSFORMATIONS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE NETFLIX SERIES BETTER THAN US
items.abstract: Rapid technological advancement in the twenty-first century has resulted in alteration of s the relationships between humans and machines which further results in reshaping perceptions of cognition. In the current era, artificial intelligence is progressing in various domains blurring the boundaries between human and technology and reshaping the perceptions of cognition, consciousness and identity. The series Better than us explores the themes of artificial consciousness, human dependence on technology and reconfiguration of emotional and cognitive capacities. A number of studies have examined Artificial intelligence in literature, films and dramas, however limited research has explored the cognitive impacts of human dependence on artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. Thereby using Catherin Belsey’s textual analysis model under the broader umbrella of Hayles post humanist theory the current Study aims to explore the representation of cognitive transformations in humans through artificial intelligence in the series Better Than US. The findings of the study reveal that the series Better Than Us presents artificial intelligence as a transformative force which reshapes human ethical cognition. The series transform the traditional assumption that moral judgment and authority belong exclusively to humans. The character representation of Arisa demonstrates the role of AI systems in decision making, legal interpretation, and protective actions. This results in a redistribution of ethical responsibility between humans and intelligent machine. The analysis further elucidates that human characters gradually begin to negotiate morality within technologically mediated environments where machine reasoning influences social and institutional structures. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Human-Machine relations, Posthumanism, Better Than Us.

items.title: A Review of Human-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities
items.abstract: Abstract The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human-centric perspective, i.e., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human-centric construction manufacturing. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems.

items.title: A risk-informed urban low-altitude air network planning method under large language model guidance
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of urban air mobility calls for safe low-altitude corridor networks across complex urban airspace, where heterogeneous positioning uncertainties caused by navigation and communication errors elevate collision risk and constrain both route feasibility and network-wide connectivity. To address this issue, this study proposes a risk-informed network planning framework that integrates three-dimensional collision risk modeling with language-model-guided multi-agent learning for the construction of safe urban air corridor networks. Specifically, a three-dimensional collision risk map is first constructed by translating navigation and communication errors into spatially varying positioning uncertainty, providing a unified safety basis for route feasibility evaluation. Network construction is then formulated as a cooperative graph connectivity task on the risk map, in which multiple learning agents jointly balance route connectivity, construction cost, and accumulated collision risk through coordinated training and distributed execution. To further accelerate convergence in complex urban environments, a vision-language model interprets airspace structure and produces high-level priors that steer agents toward safer altitude regimes. A case study over the low-altitude airspace of Nanjing demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework in producing risk-compliant air corridor networks, with language-model-derived priors further reducing training effort by 50.3 %. The results support safer and more systematic air network strategies in complex urban environments, contributing to evidence-based collision risk mitigation and airspace management in the emerging urban low-altitude economy.

items.title: A robust and reliable method for malware classification using hybrid features and gradient boosting
items.abstract: The most significant problem facing software security firms in the current cybersecurity system is the fact that new strains of malware keep on appearing. The achievement of successful detection of malicious software based on both static and dynamic data remains unmet despite the further realization of different approaches to deep learning and machine learning. Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power (particularly GPUs) and time. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets. A classification model based on gradient-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in-distribution test samples well. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98.10 and 98.40% using combined datasets. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems.

items.title: A survey on intelligent transportation systems for accident detection and risk prediction using AI
items.abstract: The complexity of today's transportation networks has made road safety, accident detection, and risk management increasingly challenging. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer a technological base to enhance transportation safety by incorporating sensors, communications, data processing, and intelligent decision-making. This review discusses the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for accident detection and risk prediction in ITS by examining information sources, methodologies, accident investigation, and associated challenges. It examines the use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal modeling, and multimodal AI for accident detection, risk prediction, severity analysis, and active safety management. This review of studies suggests that collecting traffic, vehicle, road, environmental, geographical, historical, and driver-related information can improve understanding of collisions and support timely safety decisions. The review also highlights the importance of explainable and reliable AI that provides transparency, dependability, and accountability. However, the obstacles include data heterogeneity, model generalization, dynamic conditions, scalability, quick implementation, privacy considerations, security requirements, and compatible information systems. In conclusion, incorporating AI in ITS may have the power to shift road-safety management from reactive measures to data-driven approaches.

items.title: A systematic workflow for utilizing and evaluating large language models in public health policy framing analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background For public health policy research, it is crucial to monitor policy debates to inform evidence-based policymaking. One popular method is to analyze the news for salient frames used to argue for or against a controversial topic. However, this method is time and resource-intensive since domain experts need to manually analyze relevant articles to identify frames. This study presents an approach for using large language models (LLMs) to extract frames and to systematically evaluate results. Methods Building on the results of a framing analysis of the German media debate about a tax on animal-based foods, we developed a systematic workflow to utilize LLMs to extract all instances of the 10 most frequent manually coded negative frames from 46 news articles. With one prompt per article in a few-shot setting we generated a list of quote/frame pairs. We then evaluated results against human-coded ones and calculated precision, recall, and F1-score. Results GPT-5 achieved 79.8% precision and 79.8% recall, identifying 75.2% of manually coded frames. Extracted quotes generally aligned with human-extracted text sections. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview yielded higher precision but lower recall, resulting in a comparable F1-score (79.0% vs. 79.8% with GPT-5). These findings suggest the approach is generalizable across different frontier models. Conclusions This study introduces a workflow for LLM-assisted frame extraction and transparent evaluation against an expert reference standard. Integrating this approach into public health policy coding can save resources and accelerate analysis. Ultimately, this could increase the representativeness and timeliness of data, enhancing our understanding of ongoing public health policy debates.

items.title: Advances in Reconstructive Plastic Surgery: From Skin Grafts and Microsurgery to Tissue Engineering, Artificial Intelligence and 3D Bioprinting — A Narrative Review of Evolution, Clinical Applications, Emerging Technologies, Challenges and Future Directions
items.abstract: Reconstructive plastic surgery has evolved from relatively simple techniques of wound closure and skin replacement into a multidisciplinary field capable of restoring increasingly complex anatomy and function. Skin grafts and local or regional flaps remain indispensable because they are reliable, accessible and clinically established, while microsurgery has expanded the ability to transfer vascularized tissue to defects created by trauma, burns, cancer, congenital anomalies and other conditions. At the same time, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine have introduced a different objective: rather than merely replacing missing tissue, the field increasingly seeks to recreate biological environments that support regeneration, vascularization, innervation and long-term functional integration. This narrative review examines that transition and integrates conventional reconstructive surgery with contemporary advances in biomaterials, stem-cell-based therapies, tissue-engineered skin, vascular and nerve engineering, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting, digital surgical planning, artificial intelligence (AI), robotic microsurgery and emerging digital-twin concepts. Particular attention is given to the persistent translational barriers that separate promising laboratory demonstrations from routine clinical treatment, including vascularization, cell survival during printing, innervation, immune response, mechanical integration, long-term durability, manufacturing, cost and regulatory uncertainty. AI is examined as an enabling technology rather than a replacement for surgical judgment, with applications in virtual surgical planning, image analysis, flap-risk prediction and postoperative monitoring. Evidence summarized in the supporting research material indicates that virtual planning can improve geometric accuracy and that machine-learning systems may assist in risk stratification and monitoring, but external validation and prospective clinical evaluation remain essential. The review concludes that the most credible future is not the disappearance of conventional reconstruction but the convergence of microsurgery, regenerative biology, advanced biomaterials, computational planning, AI and biofabrication.
